detail.title: The Two-day Close: Shop-floor Discipline and AI Estimation in Two Iranian Manufacturing Plants

detail.abstract: Purpose-Manufacturers often wait a week or more for monthly financial statements, because cost accounting depends on shop-floor data and late supplier documents. This paper shows how two Iranian manufacturing plants cut the time to issue monthly financial statements to two days after month-end. Design/methodology/approach-A practitioner case study of two plants, Yazd Separ and Morvarid Powder, written by the practitioner who led the change. The intervention combined shop-floor process redesign, an advanced accounting architecture (reverse chart of accounts, self-governing sub-ledgers, and floating detailed accounts), an automated 13-step close run with a validation gate in the MR-Correct ERP system (deployed across more than 1,500 corporate clients), and AI-based estimation of late-arriving costs such as energy, water, overtime and incentive pay. Close cycle time is compared before and after, and against APQC benchmark data. Findings-Both plants now issue monthly financial statements two days after month-end, down from about 15 days, and have held that pace for seven consecutive months. Two days is 58% below APQC's topquartile threshold of 4.8 calendar days and 69% below its median of 6.4 days. The automated run takes about five minutes of machine time; the rest of the close goes to resolving data exceptions. Research limitations/implications-Two plants, a before-after design and a practitioner-author who holds equity in both plants and founded the software vendor limit generalisation. APQC's measure covers consolidated statements in mostly larger, multi-entity firms, so the comparison is indicative rather than exact. The accuracy of the AI estimates has not yet been measured. Practical implications-Mid-sized manufacturers can reach a world-class close without a global ERP suite. The decisive moves are recording at source, automating the close behind a validation gate, and replacing waiting with estimates that are trued up every month. Originality/value-Most fast-close evidence comes from large multinationals with enterprise software, such as Cisco. This case documents a shop-floor-led route in a high-inflation, resource-constrained economy, and specifies where AI fits in the close.

detail.abstract: Municipal solid waste management in Ghana's Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) is structurally vulnerable to procurement corruption, supervisory capture, and performance monitoring gaps that conventional audit mechanisms have failed to close. This paper proposes a permissioned-ledger enforcement architecture that combines Hyperledger Fabric, Chaumian blind signatures, Groth16 zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs), and a tiered gig economy incentive structure to automate contractor accountability without exposing community monitors to identification or retaliation risks. The system design includes a hardware-stratified logger model that accommodates the realistic device landscape of target communities, a cryptographically verifiable infraction pipeline from photographic evidence captures through smart-contract penalty disbursement, and a legal barrier framework that sequences implementation against eight named hard-gate prerequisites. The paper addresses the full threat surface of the proposed system, including logger collusion risk, trusted-setup governance for the Groth16 ceremony, node-liveness dependencies, escrow-custodian licensing under the Banks and Specialised Deposit-Taking Institutions Act (Act 930), and anti-surveillance operational design for community monitors. Policy implications for MLGDRD, the Bank of Ghana's regulatory sandbox, and the Cybersecurity Authority of Ghana are developed alongside political transition provisions for a system whose deployment timeline spans an electoral cycle.

title: A Discussion of the Societal Impact of AI Bias in Football Scouting

detail.title: A Discussion of the Societal Impact of AI Bias in Football Scouting

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I would like to express my sincere gratitude to my mentor, Kishwar Iqbal, for their guidance, supervision, and continued support throughout this project, as well as for the many valuable discussions that helped shape this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted independently without external funding, grants, or institutional financial support.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is becoming increasingly popular in football scouting due to its efficiency and objectivity; however, a machine learning model trained on historical data about football players is likely to exhibit a relative age effect (RAE) pattern that the system will continue to reproduce. In this research, we investigate whether an AI-based football scouting system could be biased against young or late developers and discuss the possible ethical, social, and economic consequences of age-based discrimination. Transfermarkt data was processed in Python using a distribution comparison and a chi-square test. A positional heatmap was built to demonstrate the relative age effect (RAE) in the dataset, revealing that the bias is higher in physically developed positions, such as center back and defensive midfield, with a Q1:Q4 ratio of 1.99. The presented analysis could help create position-specific correction coefficients for future AI models, enabling algorithms to correct historical relative age bias rather than reproducing it in new assessments. Therefore, the main threat seems to be selection and visibility bias that occurs before applying any AI technologies, as well as the use of position-specific bias measures in the future.

detail.abstract: Access and benefit-sharing (ABS) is often dismissed as unworkable, yet this perspective argues from practical experience that it can be a genuine win-win for providers, companies, and science. Twelve years after the Nagoya Protocol’s adoption, slow permitting, downstream renegotiation demands, joint-IP requirements, and above-norm royalty expectations push companies toward freely available digital sequence information (DSI), while provider authorities face more institutional risk from granting access than from refusing it. The authors propose addressing ABS risk fully, once, at the point of access, with a single company carrying the benefit-sharing obligation for the entire downstream value chain. Basecamp Research serves as a proof of concept: more than 200 partnerships in over 30 countries, over 130 royalty payments to partners in 21 countries, and royalties triggered by data-derived revenue and allocated through provenance tracking of AI training data, at rates reported as more than ten times those indicated for the Cali Fund. The paper calls for reciprocal commitments: provider countries can exercise sovereignty through clean IP terms, defined timelines, and industry-standard royalties, while companies accept downstream obligations, invest in local capacity, and maintain traceability. Done well, the authors conclude, ABS becomes a competitive advantage rather than a tax on innovation, and generative biology a major benefit-sharing opportunity rather than a loophole.

title: The Symbiotic Intelligent Supply Chain Redefining the Intelligent Supply Chain: Intelligence as a Way of Deciding

detail.title: The Symbiotic Intelligent Supply Chain Redefining the Intelligent Supply Chain: Intelligence as a Way of Deciding

detail.abstract:
The intelligent supply chain has become a major strategic concern. Disruptions,
geopolitical crises, volatile demand, regulation, sustainability pressures and the
arrival of AI agents force supply chains to rethink how they source, produce,
deliver and decide. Most research asks how to introduce artificial intelligence,
digital twins and control towers, and assesses the result firm by firm, through
technology and operational gains. Few ask what makes a supply chain
intelligent. Many supply chains use AI widely and still execute decisions whose
conditions have expired.
This paper proposes that intelligence belongs to decisions, not to tools or data:
data and information can be correct, timely and complete, but only a decision
can be intelligent. A decision is intelligent when it starts from the right question,
rests on conditions that still hold and is taken, or changed, at the right time.
Intelligence is therefore temporal: an adverb for how decisions are taken, not an
adjective for a firm or a supply chain. Supply chain intelligence is the emergent
capacity of all the parties of a supply chain, acting together, to ask the right
questions and to take, connect, keep valid, change in time and learn from their
consequential decisions. It is symbiotic, first between the parties and then
between people and AI, and it is assessed for the supply chain itself, not for its
leading firm.
The Symbiotic Intelligent Supply Chain (SISC) achieves this intelligence through
three layers: a strategic layer that renews direction through a continuous,
conditional SWOT of the extended supply chain; a partnership design layer,
decision ergonomics, that shapes how people and AI decide together; and a
runtime layer that adapts that partnership to normal, alert, crisis and recovery
states. Verified decision evidence supports an assessment of question integrity,
validity, timeliness, memory and learning for each party, at their interfaces and
for the network. Decision-Making Driven Design (DMDD) supplies the applied
architecture and Unified Symbiotic Intelligence Science (USIS) the theoretical
foundation. An illustrative design case compares an appliance supply chain,
from its magnet suppliers to its export markets, before and after; it claims no
implementation and no measured result. The paper is a conceptual research
study: it identifies a gap in how supply chain intelligence is defined and
assessed, develops a proposition to fill it, and sets out research questions for
testing it in multi-tier supply chains.

detail.abstract: Regulated life sciences organizations have spent more than a decade learning to validate their data infrastructure. Governed data lakehouses, medallion lineage, immutable audit trails, and risk-based Computer Software Assurance now give auditors a defensible, traceable path from a regulatory submission back to the raw source record [1, 2, 13, 14]. That is a genuine achievement. It is also widely mistaken for something it is not: assurance that the artificialintelligence systems now making and informing decisions on top of that data are themselves trustworthy. This paper argues that validated data infrastructure and trustworthy AI decisions are different problems, separated by what the author terms the GxP-AI governance gap: the distance between a platform whose data lineage is validated and a decision whose model behavior is not. Drawing on the clinical-validation literature, which has long distinguished algorithm testing from clinical validation [3, 4, 5], the paper shows why the governing GxP principle-that the record must reflect reality-breaks when a model sits between the data and the decision, and why the major AI-specific regulatory instruments [6, 7, 8, 9, 10] already presuppose a correspondence that a validated platform alone does not establish. It then specifies a deployment-time assurance layer, reframing data lineage as decision lineage, that closes the gap.

detail.abstract: The rise of cryptocurrencies has prompted nonprofit organizations (NPOs) to explore crypto donations as a supplementary revenue stream. While some manage the process in-house, most rely on third-party platforms that offer operational convenience but entail subscription fees, commissions, and limited flexibility in donor engagement and liquidation timing. This study evaluates whether NPOs should adopt crypto fundraising and, if so, whether it should be self-managed or outsourced. We develop an analytical model of net yields and the surplus from transitioning to selfmanagement. Using data from 69 crypto fundraising campaigns, we estimate a predictive model of donation behavior based on token characteristics and market conditions and embed it in a simulation framework under alternative governance modes and liquidation policies. Results show that crypto fundraising is worthwhile under either governance mode and at every donation level we consider, so the adoption remains attractive regardless of the implementation mode. Conditional on adopting, self-management increases expected net yield even under immediate liquidation, through fee avoidance alone, as long as its internal cost stays below a break-even level. Additional gains arise when self-managed NPOs retain donated cryptocurrency rather than liquidate it immediately, more than doubling expected net yield, mainly through historical cryptocurrency appreciation, although holding exposes them to downside risk and can underperform immediate liquidation in unfavorable markets. The analysis identifies two main sources of surplus: fee avoidance, which under our cost assumptions matters most for smaller NPOs, and asset appreciation from holding, which generates the largest gains for larger NPOs when postponed liquidation is feasible.

detail.abstract:
A global Microsoft 365 outage on 12 and 13 November 2026 revived the question of whether NHS organisations should bring systems back on-premises. This paper argues that the better question is what minimum of care must remain possible, for which patients and for how long, when shared digital dependencies fail, and who must demonstrate it.

Drawing on the public record of the outage, the 2026 military strikes on cloud data centres, NCSC reporting on state-linked cyber activity, the 10 Year Health Plan, national emergency preparedness arrangements, and current clinical safety, medical device, cyber and data law, it proposes Isolation Tiers: a classification of clinical and operational capabilities by minimum clinical service, isolation endurance, recovery tolerance, safe capacity and recovery integrity.

The architecture is cloud-centred with a deliberately engineered local layer. It is assessed at site, provider and population-service level, governed through a dependency register, and tested through exercises at each level. It separates what a trust can decide from what rests with suppliers and national bodies, and asks DHSC for common digital-disruption planning assumptions and demonstrated survivability of national platforms.

detail.abstract: The global healthcare system faces unprecedented challenges due to aging populations and workforce shortages, particularly in long-term care. This position paper explores how Actionable eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (AxAI) can enhance public health policy by improving the predictability, fairness, and rationality of workforce decision-making. Two warnings frame the argument: the exodus of junior doctors in South Korea from 2024 to 2025, which ended after the government reversed an admissions increase criticized as lacking clear scientific evidence, and the global nursing shortage. I then introduce Park’s Optimized Nurse Staffing (Sweet Spot) Estimation Theory-driven AI-integrated Decision-Making Support System, which is designed to identify clear thresholds of optimal safe staffing levels, maximizing quality relative to cost. Where the cost a patient bears rises with staffing, this objective can have an interior optimum, which no proxy in which more is always better can locate. I situate AxAI among explainable AI, algorithmic recourse, and evaluative AI, and argue that it extends them in three ways: its actions are addressed to patients and caregivers who choose among institutions; the objective that generates them is theory-derived and patient-defined; and the actions of many patients, taken together, become incentives to which institutions respond, which turns explanation into a problem of mechanism design. Limitations include algorithmic bias, strategic manipulation of reported measures by institutions, and the inability to capture human emotion, creativity, or cultural preferences; AI should not be relied upon to create ethical norms or standards. I close with three questions on which the proposal stands or falls.

Nevertheless, a central design question in IS research remains unresolved: how should diagnostic responsibility be allocated between the learner and the AI tutor to foster, rather than replace, learner reasoning? This study identifies tutor initiation as a critical design dimension in LLM-based tutoring that redistributes diagnostic responsibility between the learner and the system. A controlled experiment with 90 students revealed no average treatment effect but demonstrated substantial heterogeneity in conceptual reasoning: proactive initiation benefits novices by accelerating error diagnosis, whereas reactive initiation supports advanced learners by preserving self-diagnosis. detail.abstract: Purpose. This paper reviews how artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping on-page search engine optimization (SEO) and what this implies for small local service businesses in Indonesia. Design/methodology/approach. A structured literature review was conducted on sources published between 2020 and 2025, drawn from international publishers (Elsevier, AIP Publishing, Emerald, IGI Global, Springer, ACM), preprint servers (arXiv, SSRN) and Indonesian journals. After screening and reference validation, 18 sources were synthesized thematically into four pillars: semantic optimization, AI-assisted content production, technical and visual optimization, and human oversight for E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness). Two Indonesian businesses, Rawatin (a local care-and-repair service marketplace) and Lavithra (a custom apparel printing service), are used as illustrative cases rather than as empirical tests. Findings. The literature consistently describes AI as useful for intent analysis, content drafting, metadata and structured-data tasks, and real-time optimization. Quantitative evidence is narrower than commonly claimed. Experimental work shows that generative engine optimization (GEO) techniques can raise source visibility in generative engine responses by up to 40% on a benchmark, and an observational study links metadata, semantic HTML and structured data to citation by AI answer engines. A controlled comparison, however, found that human-written website content outperformed AI-generated content on both search visibility and perceived quality. Across studies, human oversight is presented as necessary to manage factual errors, content homogenization and localization gaps. Originality/value. The paper consolidates recent, partly scattered evidence on AI in on-page SEO, separates experimentally supported findings from practitioner claims, and translates them into a cautious, human-in-the-loop roadmap for Indonesian micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).

title: Regulatory Naming and Shaming and Product Innovation: Evidence from App Portfolios

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA

detail.abstract: Governments and digital platforms have introduced a range of regulatory measures to combat privacy violations and infringements of user rights within mobile app markets. However, how these interventions shape developer innovation remains underexplored. Exploiting a Chinese government policy that publicly identifies apps violating users' rights as a quasi-natural experiment, we examine how regulatory naming and shaming (RNAS), a targeted, ex post intervention, affects developer innovation. Using panel data on iOS apps, we combine propensity score matching with difference-indifferences estimation and find that RNAS reduces major update activity in named apps by approximately 27.5% while increasing it by approximately 16.7% in non-named apps operated by the same developers. We provide evidence that reputational damage and regulatory concerns may contribute to reduced innovation in named apps, whereas within-portfolio resource redeployment may drive innovation gains in non-named apps. Innovation declines are larger in named apps with weaker market positions, whereas gains are larger in non-named apps with stronger positions, consistent with strategic resource redeployment. These effects persist over time. RNAS also shifts new app launches away from affected categories to other categories without affecting the total number of launches. Our findings reveal how targeted regulatory disclosure reshapes innovation within developers' portfolios and inform the design of disclosure policies that balance user protection and innovation incentives.

detail.abstract:
This paper proposes a function-level assurance method for organisational restructuring, combining an evidence-based capability case with a witnessed operational test and a post-transfer review. Its purpose is to distinguish administrative transfer, demonstrated operational capability and sustained functional performance, and to make dependencies and evidential limits explicit.

Government already holds standards for project delivery, digital operations, analytical quality and functional assurance. Existing gate, sourcing and service-transition guidance addresses operational readiness, handover and inter-organisational transition. This paper examines whether a bounded function-level evidential protocol adds value where the receiving accountable organisation must demonstrate capability after transfer.

The proposed assurance instrument is one component of a wider functional-transfer methodology; it does not prescribe the entire design or execution of a transfer. The method is illustrated twice. It is applied retrospectively to the transfer of NHS Digital’s statutory functions to NHS England in February 2023, where an evidence matrix reports what the public record establishes, what it cannot reach, and what a witnessed test would have required. It is then specified prospectively against the expectation that every integrated care board has an intelligence function in place by March 2027.

The study is a conceptual synthesis and an instrument design, with a retrospective documentary application and a prospective worked specification. The method is proposed and unvalidated. No live witnessed test has been run, and the thresholds suggested here are design requirements rather than empirically established criteria.

detail.abstract: This treatise establishes The Foundation of Knowledge Theory, a deductively closed, rigorously formalized epistemological and ontological architecture designed to solve and dismantle Agrippa's Trilemma and the Principle of Radical Doubt, while constructing the objective foundation for the Triad of Balance unifying Empirical Science, Analytic Philosophy, and Rational Theology. Proceeding strictly in progressive deductive sequence so that every formal term and symbol is grounded prior to its deployment, the monograph advances across seven interlocking chapters: to prove "Three Impossibilities of Denial"—that in any valid discourse one cannot disprove understanding, cannot disprove our actual existence, and cannot disprove absolute existence.

keywords.keywords: information continuum; Euler’s number; Einstein; Landauer’s principle; Bekenstein bound; Boltzmann entropy; Shannon entropy; path integral; de Sitter horizon; mushroom bodies; Kenyon cells; cerebellar granule cells; coincidence detection; eligibility trace; quantum error correction; cosmic web; connectome; Feynman; Herculano-Houzel; Maestro Model

detail.abstract: This essay argues that information is not a description laid over matter and energy but a third quantity in the same physical ledger, convertible with the other two at fixed exchange rates. Einstein’s c² converts matter to energy. Landauer’s kᴮT ln 2 converts energy to the erasure of a bit. Bekenstein’s bound and the holographic principle convert energy and room into the maximum information a region can hold. Boltzmann’s and Shannon’s logarithms convert information into entropy. Because every one of those laws — and Feynman’s path integral besides — is written in the base of the natural logarithm, the letter e turns out to be the signature of the whole: it marks every process whose rate is proportional to its present state, which is to say every process that is memoryless, from the gating of an ion channel and the decay of a synaptic eligibility trace to the evaporation of a pheromone trail and the exponential expansion of a universe dominated by its cosmological constant. On that foundation the essay traces four operations — acquiring information (coincidence detection), processing it (constrained state transformation), preserving it (error correction), and transmitting it into regions of time and space not yet reached (propagation under causal and horizon limits) — across some forty orders of magnitude: quantum-gravitational models of spacetime, the cosmic web, the human cerebellum, the ant mushroom body, and the signaling machinery of the cell. For each proposed parallel the mathematical object on each side is named and the relation graded as metaphor, analogy, or isomorphism. Four rows reach isomorphism or stronger, one of them an identity of physics; five are analogies with a stated shared definition; one is a conjecture awaiting its test. The essay closes by applying the ledger to itself: an essay produced by a human directing several language models is a physical object with a worldline, an erasure cost, and a light cone, and the scholarly preprint is a late and deliberate instance of the same four operations by which an ant colony straightens a trail. A provenance note records the method.

detail.abstract: The Federal Reserve's dot plot is a panel of policymakers' interest-rate forecasts. Using every dot plot from 2012 to 2026 and identified participant projections for 2012-2020, I evaluate the dots as forecasts. The median dot beats no-change and market forecasts within the year but not beyond, and it overpredicted the current-year policy rate in 13 of 14 years. Disagreement among participants is not forecast uncertainty: it does not predict the size of forecast errors or, out of sample, future rate volatility, and it is unrelated to private forecasters' disagreement. Board governors forecast more accurately than Reserve Bank presidents, but their advantage shrinks under presidential pressure as they raise their dots relative to the median. Markets nonetheless price the Fed-specific part of disagreement as policy risk. The results inform the debate over discontinuing the dot plot.

detail.abstract: I estimate how adult children's employment, earnings, caregiving, and household finances change following the first reported parental memory-related disease. Using the RAND Health and Retirement Study from 1998 through 2022, I construct a stacked event-study design that compares affected respondents with weighted comparison respondents observed over the same event window. These are reduced-form changes around a survey report, not a verified clinical onset. Employment falls gradually after the report: by 2.5 percentage points on average over the post-event period and by 4.0 points four years later. The care response follows a different path. The probability that the respondent personally provides parental care rises by 8.3 points on average, and reported personal-care hours, including documented zeros, increase by 0.9 hours per week; both responses are largest in the reporting wave and recede thereafter. Inverse-hyperbolic-sine earnings also decline, although estimates in dollars and among positive earners are imprecise. I find no detectable short-run change in household net worth. Usual weekly work hours, assigning documented nonworkers zero, decline by 1.1 hours, while hours among current workers and reported retirement do not change significantly. Employment is the clearest observed labor-supply margin. Within reciprocal treated spouse pairs, I find no detectable own-parent versus in-law difference in employment changes. The employment decline grows as the initial care response recedes.

detail.abstract: Coherence and robustness pull against each other in risk measurement. We make the tradeoff exact inside the two-parameter incomplete-Beta family of distortion risk measures, whose members are expected order statistics: ρ a,b (X) = E[X (a:a+b-1) ], the expected b-th worst of a+b-1 draws. Reparametrised by an anchor τ and a concentration ν, the coherent members form a wedge bounded by the proportional-hazard and dual-power transforms; coherence and a bounded influence function are mutually exclusive for every tail index; and on the coherent wedge the Krätschmer-Schied-Zähle index of qualitative robustness equals b. In k-of-n terms the price of coherence is one order statistic: worst-of-n is the only coherent sampling rule, while discarding the single worst of three or more draws gives bounded influence for every finite-mean loss. Trimming has a second price, in calibration: the number of draws at which a trimmed rule reproduces expected shortfall depends on the tail without bound. On seven equity, currency and commodity series through 2025, discarding one order statistic reduces the effect of the largest loss by a factor of 2.4 to 7.6 at a fixed anchor, but at equal capital leaves overall precision unchanged; and, as expected for tail indices above about two, no rule, coherent or trimmed by up to three order statistics, fails to diversify on observed portfolios of up to seven assets.

detail.abstract:
We propose an annual progressive tax on high-value residential property. Each jurisdiction ultimately would set thresholds relative to a typical home value in that jurisdiction. Even if the owner moves their domicile, the parcel remains within the taxing jurisdiction. Obviously its taxable value may change with prices, construction, subdivision and changes in use. We show that, depending on how much of the future tax buyers price in, the choice of brackets makes such a tax run the gamut from an ongoing significant source of revenue to, in effect, a wealth tax on what the ultra wealthy hold in their trophy homes.

In particular, for California, we provide a model constitutional amendment to Article XIII A whose threshold, bands, and rates are left as parameters for drafters to set according to what the polity wants to achieve. We give a potential calibration with a three-band annual surtax on residential property (at 2, 3, and 4 percent on value above ten, twenty, and thirty times the statewide median). The amendment also modifies Proposition 13 to restore part of the ordinary assessment above the entry threshold. Each rate applies marginally.

detail.abstract: Council members may oppose development to protect their own homes or to represent nearby constituents. I study 489,203 rezoning roll-call records from 238 U.S. jurisdictions and 137,547 comments on land-use petitions. A member is 0.54 percentage points more likely to vote against a site assigned to her district, controlling for home proximity and member and roll-call fixed effects. It increases with the share of nearby voters in her district and with the share of her nearby constituents classified as likely opposition commenters from ownership and voter characteristics. detail.abstract: A well-run nonprofit allocates resources where they do the most good, while ensuring sufficient funding for these high-value programs, even as conditions change. When expenses rise or revenue falls—potentially jeopardizing important work—an endowment should help bridge budgetary gaps. But in order for an endowment to play this stabilizing role, endowment managers need to consider how future expenses, donations, and revenue from the mission might change, as well as correlations among them. Therefore, this Article urges nonprofits not to manage their endowment in isolation. Instead, they should account for future expenses, mission revenue, and donations. To operationalize this “big picture” approach, we recommend “six Cs.” The first three account for future expenses. The first is “cash flow.” Since nonprofits invest to fund future obligations, they need to forecast these costs to be liquid at the right time. Second, in deciding whether to spend or save, nonprofits need “comparisons” —the second C—to weigh the social return from the alternatives. Third, nonprofits also have to decide how much risk to take. Along with enhancing expected returns, more risk also increases fluctuations in the budget. All nonprofits need to weather contingencies when their investment income declines, but some navigate downturns better than others. Our third C, “contingencies,” highlights the tradeoff between expected return and risk.  The last three Cs account for future revenue. The fourth, “coordination,” calls for investment decisions to account for future donations and mission revenue. Fifth, nonprofits should reduce “correlations”—the fifth C—between this other revenue and their endowment. For example, if donors mainly work in finance, the endowment arguably should underweight this sector. Finally, fundraising is influenced not only by donors’ investment performance, but also by their expenses, including personal needs and other causes. By modeling this “contribution risk”—the sixth C—we show that nonprofits can respond with three adjustments to their endowment. First, since contribution risk makes revenue riskier, nonprofits can offset it by taking less investment risk. Second, if contribution risk will reduce future donations, nonprofits should save more. Third, as contribution risk increases—making donors less likely to donate—a nonprofit should pay less attention to the investment choices of less reliable donors when managing its endowment. Many nonprofits do not use our “big picture” approach because of “three Is”: information, incentives, and implementation. For example, information about a donor’s investments can be hard to get, and endowment managers are likely to ignore this information anyway if they are evaluated solely on risk-adjusted returns. So along with proposing a better strategy, this Article highlights obstacles in its way. After all, valuable insights can be gleaned when reality diverges from theory, as in the Coase and Modigliani-Miller theorems.

detail.abstract: This working paper develops the author's DET matrix (Demos-Ethnos-Theos), proposed as a tool for diagnosing national identity and the patterns of political leadership that derive from it. Whereas the first part of the concept described the structure of identity, the second part captures its dynamics. Each of the three dimensions occupies one of three layers of identity: the core, the semi-periphery, or the periphery. The position of a dimension determines its mode of adaptation (rigid, flexible, permeable) and its type of resilience to threats (anticipatory, reactive, retroactive), and each layer has a weakness of its own. A loss affecting a peripheral dimension may lead to its reactivation, substitution, or disappearance. The model assumes that Theos serves as a normative bond, which is why its loss has the most serious consequences. Leadership is conceptualized as the capacity to change the configuration of identity, above all to shift dimensions between layers, and integral leadership as creative leadership operating with Theos located in the core and Demos and Ethnos remaining in balance in the semi-periphery. The paper also distinguishes three levels of conflict (identity, roles, and behavior), identifying core conflict as a new element in relation to role theory. The paper is theoretical in nature; hypotheses are formulated for further empirical verification.

detail.abstract:
The 2026 National Landscape Survey - Generations: Conflicts, Opportunities and the Future of Work, developed by Cornerstone Career Services in partnership with Insper Institute of Education and Research, examined how professionals from different generations perceive their relationship with work and organizations - and, above all, which factors influence their choices, satisfaction and intention to stay with or leave a company.

The study aimed at identifying current and future concerns and challenges involving intergenerational coexistence and talent management, 880 professionals answered questions structured around three central constructs: attractiveness, satisfaction and intention to leave.

Attractiveness was analyzed through five dimensions of the Employee Value Proposition (EVP): benefits, affiliation, career, job content and compensation. Satisfaction covered seven dimensions: rewards, career, leadership, recognition, meaning of work, coworker relationships and work support. Intention to leave was examined at three levels - considering, wanting and planning to leave the organization.

Within this framework, the study sought to answer four main questions: what each generation values when choosing a company; what best explains satisfaction and dissatisfaction in each generation; which attraction variables are related to satisfaction variables; and which satisfaction dimensions are related to intention to leave.

detail.abstract:
Purpose – Between FY22 and FY24, 93% of individual equity-derivatives traders in India lost money. From November 2024 the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) introduced larger contracts, one weekly expiry per exchange, upfront premium collection and expiry-day margins, alongside a higher securities transaction tax. We test what they achieved against their stated aims.

Design/methodology/approach – Using SEBI's post-implementation studies, circulars and exchange data for FY22–FY26, the change in aggregate losses is split into parts due to fewer traders and to loss per trader.

Findings – Participation fell 17.5% in FY26, the first annual decline since FY16, and aggregate net losses fell 18.0%. At FY25's loss per trader, fewer traders alone would have cut losses by ₹22,221 crore, more than the actual fall of ₹20,103 crore. Loss per trader rose 2.4%, and 87.7% of traders still lost money. Index-options premium turnover ended FY26 23.9% above its pre-measure level.

Research limitations/implications – With no untreated group and a tax rise seven weeks earlier, the results show what followed the reforms, not their causal effect.

Practical implications – Higher costs shrank the group exposed to loss without helping those who kept trading; regulators could target product choice and trading intensity.

Originality – No earlier study, to our knowledge, tests post-implementation outcomes against the circular's own objectives or measures how much of the fall in losses comes from fewer traders.

AI disclosure statement – Claude (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) was used to locate public SEBI sources, to check the percentage changes and decompositions in Tables II and III, which the authors computed from the SEBI data, and for copy-editing of text written by the authors. The authors verified every figure against the cited SEBI publications and take full responsibility for the content.

detail.abstract: Today’s AI boom is funded in part by preferential tax policies, and yet AI contributes little to the public fisc. If AI causes job loss, the tax base will take a bigger hit. But tax policy can do more than raise government revenue: taxes can drive companies to pay their fair share, make data centers bear the costs they impose on communities, discourage layoffs and speculative investment, and check power. Rather than recommend one tax approach, this paper outlines 34 ways to tax AI across local, state, and federal jurisdictions, in six categories: data center taxes, chip taxes, data taxes, AI company and product taxes, automation taxes, and general tax reforms relevant to AI. For each, the paper briefly describes the tax and relevant variants, and provides references to analyses, proposals, and laws. If policymakers fail to tax AI, it will not be for lack of options.

detail.abstract: Section 29A came into the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code through ordinance in November 2017. The problem it addressed was specific: erstwhile promoters were buying back distressed companies through resolution processes at steep discounts, despite having caused the insolvency in the first place. Under clause (c), persons whose accounts have been classified as non-performing assets for one year or more cannot submit resolution plans. A proviso allows them to regain eligibility by clearing overdue amounts before submission. The Supreme Court upheld Section 29A in Swiss Ribbons Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India (2019). Article 14 was satisfied, the Court held, because intelligible differentia and rational nexus to statutory objectives existed. But something was missing from the analysis. The petitioners had argued that clause (c) lumps together wilful defaulters with those whose NPAs resulted from sectoral downturns or policy shocks beyond their control. Justice Nariman’s response noted that Section 29A captures both malfeasant persons and those merely unable to pay. This observation restated what the petitioners were complaining about. It did not answer the complaint. The doctrinal gap is the subject of this article. Section 29A(c) is over-inclusive relative to its objective. The intelligible differentia framework lacks tools to address intra-class heterogeneity of this kind. The statutory cure mechanism does not solve the problem. And the Supreme Court’s Article 142 intervention in Arcelor Mittal India Pvt. Ltd. v. Satish Kumar Gupta, where additional cure opportunities were granted despite disqualification being established, suggests implicit recognition of what Swiss Ribbons left unexamined.

detail.abstract: Public officials in India who buy land ahead of infrastructure and zoning decisions commit no offence. In Chekka Guru Murali Mohan v. State of Andhra Pradesh (2021), the Andhra Pradesh High Court quashed prosecutions over purchases made before the Amaravati capital was notified, holding that insider trading is an offence only in securities law. The Supreme Court declined to interfere. Two press investigations from Madhya Pradesh in 2026 show the same gap in its current form: a joint purchase by about fifty civil servants near a bypass approved sixteen months later, and purchases in Ujjain by the family of a sitting Chief Minister. This paper proposes a narrowly defined offence based on the misuse of state information. It has seven elements, covering the information protected, the officials bound, the buyers connected to them, the prohibited purchase, the defences, and a disclosure duty triggered when a zone is notified. To test whether this definition can be enforced in practice, the paper builds a synthetic land registry that links invented sales, officials, their families and their companies. It adds twelve purchases modelled on the ways land was bought in the documented cases, and writes each element of the offence as a search over those records. Every purchase returns the result fixed for it in advance, and none of 300 ordinary sales is flagged. The test also marks where the design stops: a distant relative or stand-in who files a compliant declaration is not detected.

detail.abstract: Hard conditioning in regime-aware risk models creates sample gating: a small change in classifier output can replace the estimation subsample. Across two point-in-time equity universes and a sector-ETF panel, a 20% covariance review rule fires 5.6–6.4 times a year under hard selection and 0.2–0.4 under the full window. Posterior averaging of the hard selector’s own components cuts this to 2.3–3.7, reduces median transition displacement by 72–81% across six estimator classes, versus 4–37% for pooling at the selected state, and minimum-variance turnover by 23–30%, trading rare large revisions for frequent small ones. We split estimator updates into arrival (new data, fixed state input) and gating (fixed data, changed state input): with data and components fixed, selection jumps by a between-state distance, while posterior averaging is Lipschitz in the state probabilities. Against the full window, averaging lowers risk-forecast loss in all 9 comparisons: 7 significant nominally, 3 after Holm adjustment; the pooled average retains 9 after adjustment. The pooled selector beats its average significantly in 4 of 9 nominal tests. Exponential weighting forecasts better than either average in all 9 comparisons (6 significant each); both beat Ledoit–Wolf in all 6. Benchmark tests are unadjusted. A tempered posterior maps the stability–accuracy frontier.

detail.abstract:
This evidence-led synthesis evaluates 27 retirement-income and asset-allocation approaches across 48 authenticated reports, numerical tables, and calibration arrays completed through November 4, 2026. Without running new simulations or pooling incompatible study vintages, it organizes completed findings across five distinct families: foundational age-based and annuity models (2011–2022), legacy Gaussian-moment tests with mandatory floors, sampled-mortality joint-to-survivor household studies, fixed-state data-cloud and path-connection architectures, and historical market-decline behavioral counterfactuals.

Each policy is evaluated across three competing household objectives: (1) Standard of Individual Living (SOIL) continuity, measuring preservation of an age- and state-specific consumption benchmark integrating outside Social Security or pension income and survivor transitions; (2) positive real inheritance, assessing terminal capital at last death while distinguishing structural positivity from meaningful reserves; and (3) unrestrained portfolio supplemental spending, distributing full annually recalculated capacity via a 10% Iteration-Failure Rate (IFR) and rolling Survival Life Period (SLP) with the 1-1/n adjustment, without a SOIL ceiling.

The 27-approach taxonomy spans 30-year fixed-real withdrawals, fixed mixes with rolling SOIL-capacity caps, direct and adjacent-step lower-volatility rate selectors, recovery-gated rules, Bellman-style unrestricted and favorable-market-gated downside minimizers, guardrails, cash reserves, idealized protected sleeves, soft and hard terminal reserves, alternative longevity horizons, delayed review cadences, uncapped full-SOIL funding, persistent cloud-ridge selectors, sequential checkpoints, and annuity comparisons, alongside fully linked paths versus serial percentile restarts (P25/P50/P75).

Results show that spending mechanics—mandatory floors, proportional IFR caps, and multi-year dollar holds—govern depletion and shortfall risk at least as strongly as asset allocation. For SOIL continuity, favorable-market-gated downside allocation and fixed 50/50 best reduce-squared shortfalls across 576 household holdout cells, while cash reserves and local rate-maximizers fail to reduce lifetime gaps. For positive real inheritance, annual proportional rules structurally prevent exact depletion under bounded positive returns, whereas mandatory floors or full-SOIL promises restore exhaustion risk, and fixed-state checkpoints cannot establish death-date guarantees. For unrestrained supplemental spending, fully linked annual 10%-IFR/SLP distributions capture genuine pathwise cuts and cumulative income, while serial percentile restarts discard dispersion and inflate P50/P75 wealth by 1.96 to 65.63 times. Five-year allocation tables across eleven mixes confirm that late-life high-equity spending leadership reflects prior wealth compounding rather than an actionable switching rule.

detail.abstract: A decision maker who knows how to act on information can ignore it, so its value is nonnegative; one who must learn the action from data pays an estimation cost. We price this trade-off for a growth-optimal (Kelly) investor who sizes a position on a state label under a quadratic-growth objective. The oracle value of the label is a weighted dispersion of the cell Kelly fractions. With J cells, n observations and small Sharpe ratios, learning a fraction for each cell costs about (J − 1)/(2n) per period, to first order regardless of cell frequencies. The label is worth learning only when its oracle value exceeds this cost. Label noise attenuates the information by a squared correlation, an AIC-type optimism correction gives a feasible threshold, oracle reliability shrinkage never loses to pooling in the limiting experiment, and a fractional stake cuts the cost roughly with its square, up to a level correction that can matter under skewness. Simulations confirm the expansions. In US market and industry data from 1971 to 2026, full-Kelly hard conditioning lowers growth net of a 10-basis-point switching cost for every label set, while quarter-Kelly conditioning is close to pooling; evidence that the labels carry information is weak.

detail.abstract: I study the short-run bunching of capital gain realizations at the one-year holding threshold using linked Form 8949 and Form 1040 records for stock and crypto over 2015-2024. The tax elasticity is-0.525 for stock in transactions and-0.846 in dollars; for crypto it is-0.628 in dollars, while the crypto transaction elasticity of-0.147 cannot be distinguished from the specification's own fit error. Crypto bunching is clear in dollars, on the same order as stock's, but not in transaction counts, where the shortfall against stock persists at every level of trading activity, and crypto's own response is confined to its largest gains. I find that taxpayers for whom crossing the one-year holding period has no current-year value bunch at least as much as those facing a real incentive, including those with no shortterm losses to harvest, and bunching does not scale with the taxpayer's own rate gap, tracking the bracket instead, particularly for stock. The results conform to a salient rule interpretation more than a response to actual tax benefits. Though the elasticity is precisely estimated, the falsification tests show that bunching does not depend on the rate gap it is divided by, so the estimate measures a response to the threshold more than to its tax price.

detail.abstract: We examine the effects of mandated paid sick leave (PSL) on nonprofit organizations (NPOs). Using a stacked difference-in-differences (DiD) design around six statewide PSL laws that apply to all employers, we find that NPOs in these states report higher employee benefits expense after the laws take effect. Program service revenue rises by approximately the same dollar amount, and the increase is larger in NPOs with high labor intensity and in NPOs funded by government purchases of service, suggesting that NPOs pass the cost on to the consumers of their services. CEO bonus and incentive compensation declines, which suggests that executives absorb part of the cost through the discretionary component of their pay. Our results suggest that the cost of paid sick leave falls on the consumers of nonprofit services and partially on executives in the nonprofit sector.

detail.abstract: Latent factor models compress many characteristics into a few factors, in the hope of capturing the risk-return trade-off better out of sample. I compare them with a model whose factors are the slopes of Fama-MacBeth regressions, "pure-play" portfolios that each isolate one characteristic. PCA, RP-PCA, and IPCA each equal this benchmark when they are estimated on pure plays and keep every factor. With 26 characteristics, the benchmark earns an annualized out-of-sample Sharpe ratio of 4.27, and their five-factor versions fall significantly short of it, by 0.45 to 1.10. When past data choose the number of factors, the three models keep a median of 17 or more, and no model does significantly better than the benchmark. Compression is costly because most of the Sharpe ratio comes from low-variance combinations of pure plays. The literature's usual test assets, managed and characteristic-sorted portfolios, fall 1.02 and 0.91 short of the benchmark's Sharpe ratio even with all factors, because their characteristic exposures change over time. These findings leave little reason to compress the pure plays or to replace them with other test assets.

detail.abstract: The 2026 US-Israel-Iran war, which began on 28 February 2026 and disrupted Strait of Hormuz shipping, is a major test of how Middle East conflict reaches oil-importing emerging economies. India imports roughly 88% of its crude, and reportedly 45-50% of its crude imports transited Hormuz before the crisis, which makes Indian equities a decisive test case. This study examines how geopolitical risk and oil price shocks propagate into aggregate and sectoral volatility in Indian equity markets between 1990 and 2026. We combine a Kilian-type structural VAR to separate oil supply, aggregate demand and oilspecific demand shocks, TVP-VAR connectedness to trace transmission from geopolitical risk, Brent crude, USD/INR and foreign portfolio flows to the Nifty 50 and sectoral indices, and GJR-GARCH models for asymmetric volatility, with DCC-GARCH as a robustness check. A hybrid GJR-GARCH and gradient-boosting layer is evaluated for out-of-sample volatility forecasting in conflict episodes. We hypothesise that oil-specific demand shocks dominate transmission, that import-dependent and energy-intensive sectors respond more adversely than defence and upstream energy, and that rupee depreciation and FPI outflows amplify the equity response. The study contributes an oilshock-decomposed transmission account with currency and flow mediators, a sector-resolved connectedness extension to 2026, and a test of forecasting gains.

detail.abstract: When does competition among incumbents help a rival that intermediaries can adopt without leaving their incumbent? Motivated by payment cards, we study contracts with fixed fees and per-unit remuneration. When the competitive benchmark is feasible, competition can raise or lower the volume diverted to the rival, depending on the bound on fixed fees. Just below the point at which the benchmark becomes infeasible, tightening the bound lowers competitive per-unit remuneration and increases diversion. In a continuous region of the uniform-Hotelling model, the comparison with a single incumbent reverses twice along the competitive equilibrium we construct.

detail.abstract: This study aims to examine the effects of the sub-dimensions of employees' perception of digitalisation (Perceived Usefulness PU, Perceived Ease of Use PEU, Computer Playfulness CP, Computer Anxiety CA, Perceived Enjoyment PE, Job Relevance JR, Behavioural Intention BI) on motivation and job satisfaction. The research was conducted using data collected from 301 white-collar employees across various sectors in Turkey, and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) was used for analysis. Model suitability was evaluated solely on the SRMR value, in line with the literature, and the model fit well. The findings showed that PU, PEU, CP, PE, JR, and BI had significant effects on motivation and job satisfaction; CA, on the other hand, yielded unexpected results in some relationships. In addition, high R² values for motivation and job satisfaction indicate that perceptions of digitalisation account for a substantial portion of employee attitudes. As a result of this research, perceptions of digitalisation play a significant role in shaping employees' psychological well-being and influencing their overall work experience. The study contributes to both theoretical literature and organisational practices by highlighting the importance of human-centred approaches to digital transformation.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how carbon pricing affects corporate biodiversity footprints (CBF) using firm-level panel data from 2018-2024. Exploiting Washington State's Cap-and-Invest Program as a quasi-experimental shock, we combine difference-in-differences estimation with propensity score matching. We find that carbon pricing initially reduces firms' total CBF, alongside persistent reductions in air and water pollution-related pressures, while land use and resource use-related pressures increase significantly in later years. Rising resource use pressures may reflect increased demand for material-intensive technologies associated with the low-carbon transition. The increase in land use-related pressures may reflect geographical adjustments and reallocation. Heterogeneity analyses reveal stronger GHG-related improvements among firms with higher initial GHG-related biodiversity footprints and greater capital investment intensity, but weaker improvements among rapidly growing firms. Larger firms also exhibit smaller reductions in non-GHG biodiversity pressures, particularly air and water pollution. Overall, carbon pricing generates biodiversity co-benefits while potentially creating trade-offs in land and resource use.

detail.abstract: Supply-chain disruptions are costly, yet many organizations detect fragile supplier-part relationships only after operations have been affected. This study asks whether a transparent, data-driven risk framework can identify supply-chain conditions that warrant earlier operational review and resilience planning. Following a design-science approach, I develop and evaluate a framework that scores 300 synthetic supplier-part items on ten risk dimensions, aggregates them into a weighted composite score (0-100), assigns four risk tiers, applies a non-compensatory early-warning rule (criticality ≥ 4 and any operational dimension ≥ 90), and separates likelihood from impact in a priority matrix. Evaluation uses simulated disruption outcomes, interval estimates, naive baseline rules, weight-perturbation analyses, and 200 replications on independently generated datasets with all thresholds held fixed. The composite score was strongly associated with the simulated disruption rate, rs = .69, 95% CI [.62, .75], and mean disruption rates increased monotonically across tiers from .18 (Low) to .57 (High), H (3) = 125.0, p < .001, ε² = .42. The early-warning rule flagged 36 items with a precision of .42 against a base rate of .25 (lift = 1.67, p = .015) but missed 80% of disrupted items. Its value was greater on an impact-weighted outcome (lift = 2.63), whereas a matched-size cut on the composite score 2 performed at least as well on both outcomes. Findings were stable underweight perturbation and replicated across fresh datasets (mean rs = .73). The framework is internally coherent and useful as a triage screen, not a complete detector. Because data and outcomes are synthetic and thresholds were tuned in-sample, the results demonstrate methodological soundness rather than real-world predictive validity.

detail.abstract: Webs of trust that distribute a valuable periodic resource equally among "one person, one account" participants face a canonical threat: an adversary ("farmer")who acquires multiple devices and wallets to claim multiple shares (a sybil attack). This paper studies the economics of such attacks against a serverless, administrator-free platform of isolated trust networks in which wallet activation requires K vouches from established members, vouching capacity is bounded by age-graded slots, and issuance is challenged by device-cost and social-cost barriers. We present an agent-based simulation (Python, numpy 2.5.3, Python 3.13.16) modeling honest network growth and a farm that purchases vouches from honest members, calibrated with a canonical device cost of $120 and a sensitivity grid over device costs {120, 200}USD and wallets per device {1, 2, 4}. Under the baseline scenario (K = 3; slots 3/5/10; seed circle 100; farm budget 20 devices/month, cap 2000 wallets; 8 runs x 60 months), we find: (1) endogenous (unbribed) farm rings activate no wallets at all - the farm's entry is necessarily paid, making vouch purchase the primary cost barrier; (2) the farm's network share is transient, peaking at 38.6% in month 28 and declining to ~12%by month 60 as honest growth dilutes it; (3) parameter choices K = 3, generous slots (5/8/15), and seed circles of >=300 minimize farm share at equal honest growth; and (4) the break-even farm price per wallet declines monotonically and crosses $0.01 at month 39 (canonical $120 device; 53.5 at $200; 33 in the worst grid cell), implying a defended horizon of roughly three years rather than permanent immunity. We conclude that the "income < cost" security criterion is achievable on a bounded horizon, must be re-verified on horizons >=3 years, and requires demurrage and burn fees as default mechanisms in value-carrying profiles. Signatures, proof-of-work, transfer moratoriums, and fees were not modeled, so simulated farm profitability is, if anything, an upper bound.

detail.abstract: The effect of technological applications on the performance of digital transformation processes of enterprises and the psychological and organizational mechanisms through which this effect is realized have not been adequately explained. This study examines the effect of employees' Artificial Intelligence-oriented Digital Transformation Perceptions (AIDA) on Individual Job Performance (BIP) and Organizational Performance (PP) and the mediating role of motivation in this relationship. This study aims to provide a human-centered perspective by analyzing whether the impact of AI-driven digital transformation perception on employees' performance outcomes is direct or through employee motivation. The sample of this quantitative study consists of blue and white-collar employees working in banking institutions in Istanbul. Data were collected from 284 participants through a structured 26-item questionnaire. The data obtained were analyzed by Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) approach with Partial Smallest Method using SmartPLS 4 software. In the evaluation of the measurement model, Cronbach's Alpha, composite reliability (CR) and mean explained variance (AVE) values were taken into account. For the structural model, path coefficients, t-and p-values from bootstrapping, as well as SRMR, NFI, and GoF indices, were assessed. The results show that EPADT has a significant positive effect on both IBP and OP, and that employee motivation mediates the relationship between IBP and OP. These findings highlight the importance of employee motivation in successful digital transformation.

detail.abstract:
A rolling cross-asset correlation matrix can be embedded in a Euclidean metric space and analyzed through
persistent homology. A topological summary may then enter the drift or diffusion of a stochastic price model
as a lagged, observable input. This manuscript develops that construction in detail and asks two deliberately
separate questions: how sensitive is the resulting model to errors in the observed dependence structure, and
does topology add genuine forecasting information? We address the former analytically; the latter remains
an empirical hypothesis.
For standardized return vectors, the chordal correlation distance is dij = p2(1 − ρij ). A Vietoris–Rips
filtration yields a persistence diagram, whose longest finite H1 lifetime is a simple scalar feature. On a
common asset universe, bounded perturbations of the distance matrix imply bounded changes in the diagram
and its longest lifetime. When this feature conditions predictable Lipschitz coefficients in a log-price Itˆo
process, a synchronous-coupling estimate controls expected squared model-path deviations. We give explicit
constants, discuss how correlation estimation errors propagate nonlinearly, and calculate a four-asset example
under shrinkage exactly.
We additionally distinguish the topology of empirical asset geometry from the Riemannian geometry of
stochastic-volatility diffusions such as SABR. The research design specifies null controls, as-of data rules,
forecasting baselines, walk-forward tests, and criteria for rejecting the model. None of the propositions is
presented as a newly discovered general theorem. No trading profits, fitted coefficients, statistical significance,
or crash predictions are claimed.

detail.abstract: A castle, a villa on a lake, an apartment in a famous building. The listing speaks of luxury, and the asking price takes it for granted. Buyers and lenders have no yardstick for checking how much of that price is substance and how much is story. Sellers know, and the buyer pays for this asymmetry. The paper describes an independent check, carried out on public sources, that separates three things: what no one can redo; what can be redone, such as quality finishes and systems; and what the listing asserts without proof. From this comes a value range with three segments: the value of similar properties in the area, the value of replicable quality, and the share the market attributes to what is irreproducible. The last is the most uncertain, and the dossier shows it as an interval, never as a single figure. Of fifteen cases, relating to fourteen Italian properties, three show something that no one can redo: one proven, two with reservations. The others are replicable quality, recognised historic value or claims without proof. Each dossier says what is missing to change the judgement. The main reader is the buyer, the lender or the adviser. The seller can use it too, on one condition: sources and method must be open to checking, because a dossier created by the seller remains an interested source for the buyer.

detail.abstract: The present study aimed to examine the impact of inclusive leadership on employees' intention to use artificial intelligence (AI) and to test the mediating roles of psychological safety, emotional regulation, and trust in AI in this relationship. According to the model, inclusive leadership was identified as the independent variable, intention to use AI as the dependent variable, psychological safety and emotional regulation as mediating variables, and trust in AI as both a mediating and direct influencing variable. The study determined that the model met the reliability and validity criteria (CR > 0.70; AVE > 0.50; HTMT < 0.90), the structural model showed acceptable fit (SRMR = 0.079), and the explanatory power was at a moderate-high level (R² mean = 0.443; AI use intention R² = 0.619). In conclusion, the study revealed the central role of individual emotional self-regulation capacity and trust mechanisms in the AI adoption process, and demonstrated that AI acceptance is shaped not only by cognitive but also by emotional and organizational dynamics.

detail.abstract: This study examines the effect of corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives on the financial sustainability of banks in Southern African countries. Corporate social responsibility has increasingly become an important component of corporate strategy within the banking industry, influencing institutional reputation, stakeholder relationships, operational efficiency, and longterm financial performance. Despite the growing adoption of CSR initiatives, questions remain regarding their contribution to the financial sustainability of banks, particularly within the Southern African banking environment. The study focuses on the relationship between CSR investments and financial sustainability, considering initiatives relating to environmental protection, social development, community engagement, employee welfare, and corporate governance. Drawing on existing empirical literature, the study explores how CSR expenditures and disclosure practices influence financial outcomes, including profitability, financial stability, and long-term institutional performance. Previous studies have demonstrated varying relationships between CSR activities and financial performance, suggesting that the benefits of such initiatives may depend on institutional characteristics, regulatory environments, and the strategic allocation of resources (Aliamutu & Mkhize, 2024; Siueia et al., 2019; Boateng et al., 2025). The study adopts a quantitative, secondary-data-based research approach, relying on relevant empirical evidence and published financial information to examine the relationship between CSR initiatives and financial sustainability. It further considers the potential influence of bank size, transparency, and institutional conditions on the effectiveness of CSR investments. The study is expected to provide insights into how strategically implemented CSR initiatives can strengthen the financial sustainability of banks while promoting responsible business practices and sustainable economic development across Southern African countries. The findings will contribute to the existing literature by highlighting the importance of integrating social and environmental responsibilities into banking strategies for achieving long-term financial resilience.

detail.abstract: This study examines the role of corporate social responsibility (CSR) practices in enhancing customer loyalty and profitability in Southern African commercial banks. Corporate social responsibility has become an increasingly important component of banking operations, as financial institutions are expected to demonstrate commitment to ethical business conduct, environmental sustainability, community development, financial inclusion, and stakeholder welfare. The study explores how these initiatives influence customers' perceptions, strengthen institutional reputation, promote customer trust, and contribute to long-term financial sustainability. It further investigates the relationship between CSR investments and banking profitability, considering the potential benefits of improved customer retention, brand reputation, operational efficiency, and stakeholder relationships. Drawing on existing empirical studies, the research adopts a secondary-data-based analytical approach to examine the relationship between social responsibility practices, customer loyalty, and financial performance within the banking industry. Previous findings suggest that CSR engagement can contribute positively to financial performance, although the magnitude of its influence may depend on institutional characteristics, disclosure practices, investment levels, and the broader economic and regulatory environment. Studies by Aliamutu and Mkhize (2024), Siueia et al. (2019), and Oyewumi et al. (2018) provide relevant evidence of the relationship between social responsibility and banking profitability, while Wu and Shen (2013) highlight the financial implications of CSR activities in the banking industry. The study also recognizes that customer loyalty represents an important pathway through which responsible banking practices may translate into improved profitability, particularly when customers perceive banks as socially responsible, transparent, and responsive to community needs. The research is expected to provide insights into how Southern African commercial banks can integrate CSR initiatives into their strategic operations to strengthen customer relationships and improve financial outcomes. It concludes that socially responsible banking should be regarded not merely as a philanthropic obligation but as a strategic approach to building customer confidence, competitive advantage, and sustainable profitability.

detail.abstract:
This report examines how Arizona local governments make procurement decisions, identifies key challenges, and offers practical recommendations for generating greater value from public spending. Drawing on interviews with procurement leaders, a statewide survey of procurement professionals, and an analysis of local procurement codes, it describes how procurement structures, staffing, technology, and processes function across the state.

Most Arizona local governments blend centralized oversight with department-level purchasing. In many governments, procurement is treated as an administrative function or a subsidiary element of finance or budgeting, limiting its role in strategic planning. Few governments report having enough personnel to manage procurements efficiently, and many struggle to recruit qualified staff, especially outside metropolitan areas. Cooperative and collaborative purchasing have become key strategies for Arizona local governments, helping them save time, lower administrative costs, and access vetted vendors. However, shared services and joint solicitations continue to pose significant implementation difficulties.

The report presents return on investment (ROI) analysis as a tool to help governments identify reforms that deliver the greatest value for the least cost while clarifying trade-offs and making procurement decisions more transparent and defensible. It recommends treating procurement as a strategic driver of public value and strengthening systems, relationships, and data use to help Arizona local governments deliver better results for their communities.

title: Archetypal Mechanisms of Michels' Iron Law of Oligarchy in Political Parties Viewed as Missionary Organizations

detail.title: Archetypal Mechanisms of Michels' Iron Law of Oligarchy in Political Parties Viewed as Missionary Organizations
detail.abstract: The article examines the archetypal mechanisms that may contribute to the operation of Robert Michels' iron law of oligarchy in political parties analytically viewed as missionary organisations in Henry Mintzberg's sense. It argues that oligarchization should be interpreted not only through bureaucratization, the professionalization of leadership, information asymmetry, and procedural control, but also through group-dynamic and archetypal mechanisms. Within the proposed theoretical framework, ranking conflicts in primary groups may facilitate the emergence of leader-subordinate relations, the delegation of responsibility to leaders, the sacralization of leadership, the ritualization of democratic procedures, and the personalisation of political institutions. These mechanisms are interpreted as factors that can deform the standardization of norms, generate moral duality, and gradually displace the statutory democratic structure with an informal hierarchy. The approach is theoretical and interpretive rather than empirically causal; further research should therefore test the proposed mechanisms comparatively and examine whether variable organisational structures can limit the reproduction of oligarchical power.

title: Spending Fast, Governing Slow: An Operating Model for Enterprise AI Investment

detail.title: Spending Fast, Governing Slow: An Operating Model for Enterprise AI Investment

detail.abstract:
Enterprise AI spending has reached a scale that outstrips the systems meant to control it. Gartner projects $2.6 trillion in worldwide AI spending for 2026, yet 93% of organizations already report exceeding their AI budgets. The problem is not simply that companies are spending more. It is that the operating and governance models now being applied to AI investment were built for a different kind of decision, one with fewer stakeholders and more predictable returns. An AI investment evaluation depends on knowledge held separately by engineering, procurement, finance, risk, and FinOps, and no single function can evaluate it alone. Without shared criteria, comparable proposals receive different answers depending on who happens to review them. And because AI returns are uncertain in ways that cannot be easily predicted, the financial projections that normally settle such decisions cannot be used with high confidence.

This article sets out a Finance-led operating and governance model for AI investments, a strong starting point for mature enterprises facing the five most common AI investment governance challenges. It defines the organizational structure, decision rights, and roles and responsibilities, and sets out how competing initiatives should be scored against one another. It then elaborates on how capital should be released once an initiative is approved, separating two funding questions usually asked at once: whether an initiative is worth pursuing at all, and how much money it should receive. It closes by laying down principles for managing AI investments as a portfolio and for balancing governance with innovation velocity.

detail.abstract: Malaysia's race-based welfare architecture has persisted despite sustained calls for needs-based reform. This paper asks whether politically fragmented news audiences receive systematically different framing of racial policy. It uses Gaol et al.'s (2020) audience-network clusters to analyse 173 articles from 12 outlets covering three policy events: Budget 2024, the matriculation quota announcement and the PuTERA35 launch. A bilingual dictionary instrument codes Entman's (1993) four framing functions alongside Gamson-style interpretive packages. Cluster membership significantly predicts framing (Pillai's trace = 0.254, p < .001). Opposition-aligned outlets prescribe remedies far more often than BN-aligned outlets and draw more on Unity and Grievance vocabulary. BN-aligned outlets lean on government reform language and score higher on moral evaluation. Neither cluster explicitly attributes racial causes, and the differences are consistent across all three events. The findings suggest that audience fragmentation in Malaysia produces divergence in proposing what should be done (remedy) rather than explicitly saying what or who caused a problem (causation).

title: Reflections on Race, Immigration, and the Religious Dimensions of Religion

detail.abstract:
This short essay helped wrap up a conference on religion, race, and immigration held at Lund University. The principal papers focused largely on the complexities of identity rather than theological or other specifically religious questions about immigration. My reflections tried to fill that gap by attending more precisely to “the religious dimensions of religion.”

One obvious theological observation about immigration is that many religious traditions regard care for the stranger as not merely right and moral but integral to God’s own essence and to the proper ordering of the human relationship with God. Yet religious traditions can help us understand why so many societies fall short of that imperative of welcome and love.

Many conference papers offered powerful insights into colonialism, whiteness, and racialization. But a religious sensibility might reveal something else behind hostility to migrants. I do not believe in original sin, but I do believe that the temptation to sin is part of the human condition. Across times and places, that temptation often manifests itself in xenophobia and the failure to do right by those perceived as Other.

More particularly, encounters among religious traditions in places such as Europe, though often more cooperative than stereotypes suggest, have also produced centuries of struggle and a mythos of religiously inflected collective traumatic memory that still shapes attitudes and policies. Yet the best therapy for that mythic trauma might be not less religion, but more. Western memory includes not only trauma but also grace.
