detail.abstract: Some investors respond to market excitement by deliberately stepping back and being content with it, a state known as the joy of missing out (JOMO). We measure this state with a Global JOMO Index built from worldwide Google Trends searches that mirror the search terms of the Global FOMO Index: contentment with not participating, passive investing, patience, relief after sitting out, digital detox and safe saving. The index is persistent; a high-JOMO month is followed by another high-JOMO month 92% of the time. Once the common growth of internet search is removed, JOMO and FOMO move in a cycle. During the AI boom, AI hype predicts higher JOMO one to twelve months later, while JOMO does not predict AI hype. AI hype raises the returns of AI-exposed stocks, and the response is smaller when JOMO is high, although this difference is not statistically significant.

detail.abstract: The Bien Hoa to Vung Tau Expressway is a 53-kilometre route in southern Vietnam connecting the industrial base of Dong Nai to the deep-water port area of Vung Tau, with an estimated investment of 17.8 trillion VND. Economic forecasts for the project were prepared before 2018, and the regional context has changed substantially since then. This study reassesses the expected economic effects using current data and an integrated analytical framework with five components: accessibility analysis based on a gravity potential model, regional interaction modelling incorporating observed traffic counts on National Highway 51, industrial development potential assessment, economic corridor centrality analysis, and GRDP growth forecasting under a range of agglomeration elasticities. The analysis covers the four principal localities on the corridor, Bien Hoa, Long Thanh, Phu My and Vung Tau, together with Ho Chi Minh City, Phu My Port and Long Thanh Airport as connecting nodes, and uses 2024 as the base year. The set of nodes constitutes the complete corridor rather than a sample drawn from it. Three findings emerge. First, the expressway moves the primary node of the corridor northward: Bien Hoa overtakes Phu My in economic centrality, rising 104 per cent against 62 per cent. Second, industrial development potential rises most in Long Thanh, which combines a 5,033-hectare industrial land reserve with the largest accessibility gain. Third, growth distributes across the corridor rather than concentrating in one centre, with Long Thanh recording the largest percentage gain from the smallest economic base. Estimated GRDP growth ranges from 1.2 per cent under a conservative elasticity of 0.03 to 26.8 per cent under a strong elasticity of 0.4. For sustainable development the results point in two directions. Journey distances on the corridor fall 22.8 per cent in aggregate, and diverting through traffic from National Highway 51 relieves congestion that currently generates avoidable emissions. Freight movement to the region's principal port becomes shorter and more predictable. Against this, the project strengthens pressure to convert agricultural land, will generate induced traffic, and delivers benefits unevenly within each locality. Infrastructure of this scale shapes conditions for sustainable outcomes without securing them; the accompanying land use policy determines which outcome follows.

title: Who Disciplines Concentrated Power? Competition Law and Constitutional Democracy in Kenya, South Africa and Nigeria
affiliations: University of Nairobi, School of Law

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether competition law can answer the question that economic concentration poses to constitutional democracy: what follows when market power buys political influence, captures regulators and rations opportunity? It tests that question in Kenya, South Africa and Nigeria. The argument is that competition law is constitutional law by another route, and that its legitimacy depends on institutional design as much as on doctrine. South Africa writes ownership and inclusion into merger review through section 12A(3) of the Competition Act, and in Mediclinic the Constitutional Court tied the statute to the Bill of Rights. Kenya pairs a public interest test with a competition assessment, but its Authority logged 128 merger-related applications in 2024/25, of which only 30 were merger notifications. Nigeria's Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018 gives its Commission concurrent jurisdiction with sector regulators, though later legislation curtailed that reach in financial services. These variations show that one constitutional commitment yields different enforcement when the statute, the regulator and the political settlement differ. The paper advances three claims. First, enforcement indexes democratic accountability, because a regulator unable to discipline powerful firms cannot protect those without power. Second, public interest tests transform markets only as far as the institutions applying them allow, so independence, funding and appointment procedures matter as much as text. Third, sector carve-outs and overlapping mandates let concentrated actors choose their regulator, converting market power into regulatory power. Statutes, tribunal decisions, annual reports and commentary ground 2 a capture-sensitive model for assessing enforcement. The paper concludes that competition law earns constitutional standing only where it constrains private power, and that measuring that constraint should replace the counting of cases. Enforcement statistics, read alone, flatter regulators; read against ownership, prices and appointments, they reveal whom the law actually restrains. That reframes reform as a question of power.

title: Cross-sectional Identification with Heterogeneous Exposure to General Equilibrium Effects

detail.title: Cross-sectional Identification with Heterogeneous Exposure to General Equilibrium Effects

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interests

detail.abstract: Cross-sectional designs that exploit heterogeneous exposure to aggregate shocks while controlling for time fixed effects are widely used to estimate macroeconomic elasticities. I show that these designs fail to identify partial-equilibrium elasticities when exposure to the shock of interest is correlated with exposure to other aggregate variables that move in general equilibrium. I develop a test for this identification failure and a decomposition method that combines cross-sectional and time-series variation to purge general-equilibrium effects. Applying it to estimate US crosssectional fiscal multipliers, I find that accounting for the general equilibrium effects operating through monetary policy reduces the two-year multiplier from 1.5 to 1. This result highlights the need for cross-sectional identification strategies that account for heterogeneity in responses to general-equilibrium forces.

detail.abstract: Transportation transaction platforms face dual challenges: assisting users in selecting among complex, multi-attribute transportation alternatives, and supporting project-level decisions that balance competing operational and strategic objectives. This paper proposes an integrated framework that combines hybrid recommendation techniques with project decision support mechanisms for transportation transaction environments. The recommendation component synergizes collaborative filtering with knowledge-based reasoning to address the cold-start problem and to generate context-aware, personalized suggestions for transportation transactions. The decision support component extends this capability by incorporating multicriteria evaluation methods that enable stakeholders to assess project alternatives against dimensions such as cost, time, risk, and service quality. A software agent architecture orchestrates the invocation of recommendation services and the construction of decision rules, facilitating adaptive responses to evolving user requirements and market conditions. The proposed framework is evaluated through scenario-based experiments on a simulated transportation transaction platform, examining recommendation accuracy, decision quality, and computational efficiency. Results indicate that the hybrid approach improves the relevance of transaction suggestions compared to single-strategy baselines and enhances the transparency and consistency of project-level decisions. The findings contribute to the design of intelligent decision-support systems for transportation marketplaces where both individual transaction choices and broader project commitments must be coordinated.

detail.abstract: A new approach is proposed for estimating dynamic factor loadings and scores in a generalized dynamic factor model with a fixed common loading space, building on the ALgebraic Spectral Estimator (ALSE) and its unshrunk version (UNALSE). The ALSE performs low-rank plus off-diagonal-sparse regularization through nuclear-norm and entrywise absolute-value penalization with a free idiosyncratic diagonal, recovering the relevant rank and sparsity structures and providing consistent spectral and covariance estimates. The UNALSE preserves the structures recovered by ALSE while offsetting the shrinkage of the retained common eigenvalues. Separately, consistency rates are established for the ALSE-based loading matrix and for Bartlett and Thomson dynamic factor-score estimators, in sample and for fixed-horizon score propagation. Under the stated conditions, the estimated idiosyncratic covariance and the structured factor-model covariance used in Thomson's method are positive definite with probability tending to one, and their inverses are consistently estimated. A Monte Carlo study assesses finite-sample reconstruction under heterogeneous and cross-sectionally dependent idiosyncratic components, weaker factor-strength and sparsity conditions, and varying cross-sectional dimensions. An application to U.S. macroeconomic data examines patterns of macroeconomic co-movement and evaluates the forecasting performance of the estimated factor scores in an expanding-window pseudo-out-of-sample exercise.

detail.abstract: Over the past decade, the mantra of becoming "data-driven" has reverberated through the corridors of companies worldwide. As these organizations aim for lofty ambitions like digital transformation, mastering analytics, or becoming "AI-first" leaders, a foundational truth has emerged: effectively harnessing and managing data is crucial. In pursuit of these objectives, businesses have begun to revere data as a critical asset, steering their corporate cultures toward data-centric approaches and reshaping their strategies to spotlight the power of analytics. In this data-centric age, as companies make significant advancements in technology—particularly in how consumer data is leveraged to tailor and enhance user experiences through personalisation—profound questions arise concerning legal compliance and ethical considerations, especially around privacy. This dissertation explores the intricate dynamics between personalisation, achieved through behavioural analysis and data-driven customization, and its alignment with existing legal frameworks. It investigates the extent to which laws keep pace with the rapidly evolving digital landscape, where personal data has become a prime commodity. Furthermore, this research examines the diverse attitudes of consumers toward privacy, segmented by varying levels of concern and awareness, which influence their willingness to engage with personalized digital environments. By integrating theoretical perspectives, the dissertation proposes a set of pragmatic recommendations for businesses to navigate the convoluted terrain of legal obligations while harnessing the benefits of personalisation. This comprehensive inquiry enriches the scholarly dialogue on privacy and data protection and is a critical resource for policymakers and corporates aiming to ethically capitalize on user personalisation.

title: APS: Multi-resolution Neural and Linear Price-path Signals beyond Momentum in Large U.S. Stocks
affiliations: University of New South Wales (UNSW), FLAME UNIVERSITY, University of New South Wales and Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Madras

detail.title: APS: Multi-resolution Neural and Linear Price-path Signals beyond Momentum in Large U.S. Stocks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None

detail.abstract: We develop the Augmented Price-path Signal (APS), a cross-sectional stock-ranking signal constructed exclusively from past prices and trading volume, and study it in two forms: APS-Linear, a regularised linear model of 69 engineered features of each stock's monthly price path, and APS-MRCR, a multi-resolution convolutional-recurrent network that additionally processes the daily trading history. APS-MRCR comprises two convolutional-recurrent encoders of the stock's last 60 trading days and of its co-movement with the market, together with a feed-forward encoder of the monthly features; each branch produces a forecast of the return rank and of its own predictive variance, and an uncertaintyaware gate combines the branches at the level of the individual stock. Forecasts and portfolios remain monthly. For 501 large U.S. stocks over January 2017 to June 2026, a single pre-specified APS-MRCR more than doubles the rank correlation of APS-Linear with next-month returns (0.032 against 0.014). In Fama-MacBeth regressions that control for the best APS-Linear score, momentum, short-term reversal and size, the coefficient on APS-MRCR is positive and significant in all six evaluation windows under both value and equal weighting (𝑡 between 2.0 and 3.6), whereas the coefficient on APS-Linear is not. The incremental information persists across portfolio-weighting schemes and, in contrast to tree-based specifications, within the largest third of the index; its stronger portfolio effect under equal weighting is consistent with the greater weight that scheme assigns to smaller firms, where the signal is strongest. The incremental information also survives controls for a non-linear monthly benchmark and for a monthly-input version of the same network, in every equal-weighted window at the 5% level and in every value-weighted window at the 10% level, indicating that it originates in the daily resolution of the inputs. In every one of the 48 portfolio categories, the best fixed-weight combination of APS-MRCR and APS-Linear improves on its linear component and outperforms both the best linear specification and the best momentum strategy. The evidence is predictive rather than causal.

detail.abstract: In January 2021, WhatsApp announced a new privacy policy that Indian users could only accept or leave, while users in the European Union and the United States were offered an opt-out. This article asks whether the Competition Commission of India (CCI) should step in. It starts from the CCI’s finding in Harshita Chawla v. WhatsApp that WhatsApp is prima facie dominant in the market for over-the-top messaging apps through smartphones in India. It then examines whether the policy could amount to an abuse of dominance under Section 4(2)(a) of the Competition Act, 2002, drawing on CCI decisions on one-sided contracts such as ONGC and DLF. The article argues that the policy’s unilateral, take-it-or-leave-it terms support such a claim. It also argues that, because India had no dedicated data protection law at the time, competition law is a justified route for protecting consumers, and that the personal data WhatsApp collects gives it a “data advantage” that can act as a non-price barrier to rivals. It points to the German Federal Cartel Office’s Facebook decision and Japan’s guidelines on abuse of a superior bargaining position as comparative support.

detail.abstract: Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) have become the de facto gatekeepers of modern hiring, with over 98% of Fortune 500 companies and an increasing share of small-to-medium enterprises relying on algorithmic resume screening before human review. Despite their ubiquity, the parsing accuracy of these systems across diverse resume layouts remains poorly understood. This study presents the first large-scale, controlled evaluation of information loss during ATS resume parsing across five structurally distinct resume layout categories. We constructed a standardized benchmark corpus of 200 resumes-each containing identical professional content rendered in five layout archetypes: Standard Single-Column, Two-Column Professional, Table-Based, Text-Box/Sidebar, and Infographic/Icon-Heavy designs. These resumes were processed through ten commercially available ATS platforms, and the parsed outputs were evaluated against three fidelity metrics: Field Recall Rate, Text Integrity Score, and Category Mapping Accuracy. Our findings reveal substantial and statistically significant information loss correlated with layout complexity. Standard single-column formats achieved a mean composite accuracy of 94.0%, while infographic-style layouts suffered a 64.4% information loss rate, with mean composite accuracy declining to just 29.6%. Two-column layouts, often recommended by professional resume services, exhibited a 22.4% average information loss. We further identify specific failure modes including column-order inversion, text-box content omission, icon-to-text mapping failures, and table cell misalignment. These findings carry significant implications for hiring equity, as candidates relying on visually complex templates-often promoted by commercial resume builders-face systematic disadvantage in algorithmic screening. We propose a Layout Compatibility Index (LCI) framework and offer practical recommendations for both job seekers and ATS vendors.

detail.abstract: Criminal territorial control restricts mobility, market access, and the viability of small businesses. We study the staggered rollout of El Salvador's Plan Control Territorial (PCT), a geographically targeted security program, using household survey data from 2015-2025. We estimate that the PCT increased real monthly income from informal self-employment by about 13 percent. Business revenue and income per hour also increased, while reported hours showed no statistically significant change. The income gain persisted at approximately 15 percent in 2022-2025, when the PCT operated alongside the controversial nationwide State of Exception, but we find no evidence that the income differential between prioritized and comparison municipalities increased further. Nevertheless, post-2022 comparisons show larger declines in household-reported robbery or assault and greater improvements in all measures of perceived community safety in municipalities previously prioritized under the PCT. The results suggest meaningful economic returns to restoring state control.

detail.abstract: In this study, it was aimed to determine the effect of Big Data Capability (BDC) on Business Performance (BP) and the mediating role of Supply Chain Flexibility (SCF) and the moderating role of Environmental Uncertainty (EU) in this effect. The universe of the research consists of businesses that benefit from digital technologies in their supply chain processes in Turkey. An online questionnaire was applied to 301 middle and senior managers reached by convenience sampling method; the data were analyzed by Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The values for the measurement model (CFI=0.999, TLI=0.998, RMSEA<0.08) were perfectly agreed. The findings revealed that BCD had a positive and significant effect on SCF (β=0.483, p<0.001). SCF strongly affects BP (β=0.734, p<0.001), whereas the direct effect of BDC on BP was found to be insignificant (β=0.038, p=0.348). Since the indirect effect was significant (β=0.355, p<0.001), it was determined that SCF played a full mediating role in this relationship. In addition, EU has been found to have a moderator effect that weakens the relationship between BDC and SCF (β=-0.155, p=0.004). As a result, BDC does not directly increase BP; however, it develops indirectly through SCF.

detail.abstract: One agent's expenditure becomes another's income. When aggregation removes the relationships carrying that flow, microeconomic choices can become disconnected from macroeconomic outcomes. This paper distinguishes two levels of decoupling: the model first omits economic relationships relevant to its task, and its microeconomic reasoning then fails to explain the aggregate result. Drawing on entropy-governed economics, we treat transaction links, cash-flow timing, credit exposures, and local constraints as a mesoscopic layer connecting individual behavior to aggregate outcomes. The paradox of thrift shows how consistent household decisions can generate income feedback that invalidates aggregation based on fixed incomes. We interpret economic modeling as compression for a specified task and ask what the resulting representation must preserve. A target can be computed exactly if states assigned the same representation always yield the same target value. Under a specified finite-alphabet, independent-sampling communication model, reliable computation also requires the target's information rate to lie within the relevant cut capacity. This necessary condition does not supply an executable network protocol or ensure stable adjustment. Rate-distortion theory, maximum-entropy inference, graph representations, and communication complexity clarify these distinct requirements. Four applications examine thrift, systemic financial risk, crossborder networks and networked public goods, and aggregation topology. A model connects micro and macro to the extent that its compressed representation preserves the mesoscopic relationships relevant to its question.

detail.abstract: ARC [1] introduced a three-layer governance architecture for autonomous systems consisting of model safety validation, cognitive certification (CRAB), and operational authorization (LEA). While ARC defines the conditions required for deployment, it does not specify how compliance should be maintained once systems enter operational environments. This paper addresses that gap. We introduce Delta Management, a framework for continuous post-deployment governance in which the certified baseline established during authorization serves as a permanent reference state-more precisely, a certified region rather than a point. Operational compliance is defined as the measurable distance between the current system state and this certified baseline region. Governance decisions are therefore driven not by static certification status, but by continuous measurement of behavioral deviation over time. Building directly upon the ARC architecture, we introduce four extensions. First, CRAB evaluation is anchored to the worst verified behavioral deviation, with single-observation outliers quarantined pending confirmation, ensuring that demonstrated failure modes define the operational safety floor without creating a monotonically non-increasing authority that degenerates over time. Second, we replace a single AND-gated spiral trigger with a layered trigger taxonomy that distinguishes hard safety invariants, critical single-dimension overrides, confirmed multi-system spirals, and risk-weighted composite scores-each coupled to appropriately scaled governance responses. Third, we formalize safe transition as a graduated protocol that explicitly separates governance authority withdrawal from physical stop, aligned with IEC 60204-1, ISO 13850, SAE J3016, and EU AI Act Article 14(4)(e). Fourth, we introduce environmental delta as a distinct baseline validity condition: when the operational environment drifts beyond the certified Operational Design Domain (ODD), the response is recertification or ODD revision-not authority contraction-because the baseline itself has become an invalid compliance reference. Together, these contributions transform ARC from a deployment-time certification architecture into a continuous governance framework capable of monitoring, evaluating, and enforcing compliance throughout the operational lifecycle of autonomous systems. The framework is designed for explicit positioning against EU AI Act Article 72(2), which requires providers of high-risk AI systems to evaluate their continuous compliance throughout the system lifecycle.

title: Ethical Leadership and Its Effect on Organisational Trust

detail.abstract: Trust is a foundation of cooperation in organisations, and leaders' ethical conduct is among its most important sources. This paper examines how ethical leadership affects organisational trust. Using an integrative narrative review of ethical leadership and trust research, combined with a qualitative analysis of three publicly documented cases (Johnson & Johnson's response to the 1982 Tylenol poisonings, the Volkswagen emissions scandal that began in 2015, and the 2022 decision by Patagonia's founder to transfer ownership of the company to a trust and a nonprofit organisation), the paper addresses three research questions about the relationship between ethical leadership and trust, the mechanisms involved, and the benefits and risks visible in practice. The synthesis indicates that ethical leadership builds trust when it is consistent, visible, and costly to fake, and that trust cascades from senior leaders to supervisors and from there to employees. The cases show that trust is preserved when leaders act on stated values under pressure and is destroyed when incentives and targets operate without ethical oversight. The paper concludes with recommendations for practice and research.

detail.abstract: This paper argues that Canada should adopt a voluntary Decentralized Digital ID System (DDIS), in which a person’s identity credentials are stored on their own device and only the data needed for a specific, consented purpose is shared. It contrasts that design with today’s practice of copying identity data across many centralized databases. It reviews digital identity programs in the European Union, the United Kingdom and the United States, and describes Canada’s uneven progress, including Quebec’s legislation and the national standards work of DIACC and the Digital Governance Standards Institute. It addresses public concerns about surveillance and exclusion, identifies the statutes that would need updating, including the Privacy Act, PIPEDA and the PCMLTFA, and explains why verifiable digital credentials will be needed on both sides of a transaction as AI agents begin to act for people in commerce.

detail.abstract: An investor who relies on a manager's unverifiable report must decide whether to keep investing in a firm, pause, or sell. The manager wants to avoid or delay sale whatever the true state is, so he may withhold reporting or lie. Investment supplies an endogenous test of the manager's claim: cash flows arrive more often when a favorable report is true, while a dry spell can trigger sale. The investor may suspend funding while awaiting managerial information and resume investment after a favorable report. The resulting test supports informative communication despite the manager's preference for continuation. For patient parties and a range of learning parameters, an equilibrium exists in which the manager reports truthfully when the firm is worth running and otherwise mixes between lying and silence. Before a report, the investor sells at low beliefs, invests at a loss just above the sale threshold, waits at intermediate beliefs, and invests at high beliefs. Compared to the full-information benchmark, the investor may delay funding a sound firm, finance one that should be sold, or sell a sound firm after an unlucky dry spell. These costs of unverifiability concentrate near the sale threshold. The investor prefers verifiable reports, while the manager does not always.

detail.abstract: Europe's first consolidated tape for shares went live on 14 September 2026. It consolidates market information across trading venues but leaves the venues themselves unchanged. We study its effects by comparing EU stocks covered by the tape with UK stocks outside its scope, using difference-indifferences designs with a binary treatment and a continuous treatment intensity based on each stock's pre-launch fragmentation. The tape reallocates trading across venues rather than lowering trading costs. Quoted and effective spreads, price improvement, and price efficiency show no robust improvement, and displayed depth is largely unchanged. Instead, trading becomes more fragmented relative to UK stocks: the pan-European multilateral trading facilities quote at the consolidated best prices more often, and trading shifts from the primary exchanges to them, mainly in liquid stocks. At the stock level, liquidity providers earn lower realized spreads on unchanged effective spreads, consistent with the tape informing slower traders rather than market makers. None of these effects increases with pre-launch fragmentation. Consolidating information without consolidating venues thus intensifies competition between venues but, at least in the short run, does not lower trading costs.

detail.abstract: Attribute non-attendance (ANA) is the term used to describe the phenomenon where a person ignores one or more of a good's attributes while responding to a choice survey. Consequently, the choice observed may be based on an information set different than what the researcher assumes, and inferences made from the survey's results may be biased. The challenges for the researcher are to minimize opportunities for ANA to arise in the first place by ensuring a highquality experimental design, identify and account for the ANA that persists during modeling, and account for ANA properly when calculating and reporting welfare estimates. In this chapter, we define ANA, discuss its prevalence in the literature, discuss sources of ANA and steps that can be taken ex ante to mitigate it, discuss the most common methods for measuring it, discuss the relationship between ANA and welfare measures, and discuss some of the unresolved issues.

detail.abstract:
Modern decentralized ledger technology (DLT) relies on deterministic execution environments to process state updates across heterogeneous consensus networks. However, the emergence of multi-tiered, cross-chain autonomous swarm frameworks introduces unprecedented systemic risks to liquidity protocol architecture. This technical white paper presents a comprehensive forensic decomposition and structural taxonomy of a nation state class, multi-chain botnet orchestration paradigm observed executing sub-millisecond, synchronized state manipulation across eleven concurrent Execution Layer EVM and non EVM environments.

We formalize the execution mechanics of ephemeral address swarms, private transaction routing via specialized Miner-Extractable Value (MEV) relays, and high-density state locking payloads employing99.6%non-standard, custom-compiled EVM bytecode selectors. Furthermore, we present an enterprise-grade threat mitigation framework detailing real time RPC signature filtering, dynamic mempool anomaly detection, Control Flow Graph (CFG) invariant matching, and automated cross-chain circuit-breaker protocols.

detail.abstract: Pakistan has, over two decades, built a substantial formal architecture for early childhood education (ECE): policy commitments, curriculum frameworks, provincial standards and some of the largest education programmes in its history, financed with domestic and development-partner resources. Yet provision at classroom level remains uneven, and the distance between what policy promises and what a four-year-old in a public classroom actually receives is the system's defining problem. This article analyses that distance as a *delivery-chain* failure. Drawing on twelve years of practice inside Pakistan's federal programme-coordination system-as International Coordination Officer for United Nations programmes (2012-2024), as a monitoring officer for UNESCO, UNICEF and UNDP programmes, and as Deputy Secretary at the Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training (2023-2024), coordinating a development-partner portfolio exceeding US$2.2 billion-the article traces five recurring leakage points between ministry and classroom: the translation of national design into provincial systems after the Eighteenth Amendment; financing flows that stall at intergovernmental interfaces; a workforce produced through training cascades and contract insecurity; monitoring regimes that count inputs because inputs are countable; and data that circulates upward without returning to the levels where design could change. A repair agenda follows from the diagnosis: the leaks are at the joints of the system, so the repairs must be too.

title: From AI Adoption to AI-First Universities: A Human-Centred Framework for African Higher Education

detail.title: From AI Adoption to AI-First Universities: A Human-Centred Framework for African Higher Education

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.funderStatement: Self

detail.abstract:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping economies, industries and systems of knowledge production. Higher education institutions, particularly in the Global South, now face a defining choice: to remain passive consumers of AI-enabled tools or to actively redesign institutional culture, curriculum and governance around AI capabilities. This paper argues that African universities must transition from AI adoption to an AI-first university model - not as a technological reflex, but as a human-centred, augmentation-driven strategy for developing future-ready graduates.

Drawing on policy discourse, institutional practice and lived experience within African and UK academic contexts, using a conceptual and reflective analytical approach, this paper proposes a phased framework for AI-first higher education. It emphasises alignment with institutional mission, lecturer confidence, ethical governance and student agency. The study concludes that AI-first universities in Africa can enhance relevance, graduate employability and academic leadership - provided AI is framed as an enabling partner rather than a replacement force.

detail.abstract: The Sustainable Development Goals are, by design, a coordination problem: seventeen interdependent goals assigned to governments whose machinery is organised in vertical ministries, and-in federations-divided again between a centre and provinces. This article examines that problem from inside the machinery of one federal state. Drawing on the author's thirteen years (2011-2024) in Pakistan's federal civil service-including service in the Economic Affairs Division (EAD), the nodal division for external economic assistance; an appointment as International Coordination Officer for UN agencies (2012-2024); and coordination and monitoring responsibility for a development-partner portfolio exceeding US$2.2 billion, including the One UN Programme-II (US$1.8 billion, 2013-2017)-the article analyses how whole-ofgovernment coordination actually functions when it is attempted through aidcoordination machinery. It argues that coordination fails less often from absent structures than from structures that multiply without authority: forums proliferate, reporting serves donor accountability rather than domestic decision-making, provincial buy-in is sought after programme design is complete, and routine staff rotation dissolves the institutional memory on which coordination depends. The article closes with a reform agenda directed at the incentives of coordinators themselves, and considers what Pakistan's experience implies for SDG delivery in other federated developing states.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the historical origins and persistence of the culture of morality in regions where mobility is restricted by geography. I devise a measure of local isolation from land surface irregularities and unveil a robust association between isolation and various measures of morality in the World Values Survey at the subnational level, consistent with the view that isolation is positively linked with morality. I explore how isolation can explain historical differences in moral norms and values by studying its association with morality-related motifs in ethnic folklore. Additionally, I analyze data on second-generation migrants in Europe to demonstrate the persistence of the potential link between ancestral isolation and salience of moral norms and values. Finally, I test alternative explanations and provide an extensive set of robustness checks.

title: De Facto Resurgence of National Police Authority: Comparative Institutional Analysis of Intake Procedures Between the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department and the Chiba Prefectural Police

detail.abstract:
Postwar Japanese police reform fundamentally dismantled the centralized, bureaucratic apparatus of the pre-war Home Ministry’s Police Bureau (Naimu-shō Keihokyoku) in order to guarantee local decentralization and democratic civilian oversight. Central to this statutory architecture was the establishment of the Public Safety Commission (Kōan Iinkai) as a collegial civilian governing body insulated from bureaucratic self-interest. However, in contemporary administrative intake practices governing statutory requests for the disclosure of retained personal information under the Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI), an alarming procedural deviation has emerged.

This study compares the intake procedures of the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department (TMPD) and the Chiba Prefectural Police Headquarters in response to disclosure requests filed by the same requester on the same day in October 2026. The TMPD issued a dated notice citing the request’s tracking number, enclosed an explicit opt-in confirmation form addressed to the Superintendent General, and sent both by postmarked restricted delivery mail. The Chiba Headquarters issued an unauthenticated sheet of paper lacking an issuance date, document management number, the disposing authority’s name, or official seal, sent by ordinary mail without a dated postmark. It declared that the requester’s failure to object by a self-set deadline would be treated as no objection, a “deemed consent” (minashi dōi), to reassigning the addressee from the Chief of Police to the Prefectural Public Safety Commission. The Chiba request, moreover, concerned a complaint to that very Commission, including the Headquarters’ internal records.

Drawing on principal-agent theory and administrative law, this paper argues that the subordinate executive organ thereby assumed, through a fiction of silence without statutory basis, a decision reserved to the disposing authority and to the formal transfer procedure of the Act. Whatever its intent, such a default structurally functions to turn the civilian oversight body into a defensive screen for the police bureaucracy and to exclude internal supervisory records from statutory review. A timely objection defeated the deemed change on the paper’s own terms; the design defect remains. In the author’s view, it marks a de facto resurgence of pre-war national police authority at odds with the 1954 Police Act.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether capital intensity shapes U.S. firms' investment responses to two energy-market shocks: option-implied oil-price volatility and armed conflict in oil-producing Middle East/North Africa (MENA) countries. Using 1,401 non-financial firms from 2012-2024 and pre-sample PPE intensity measured separately over 2009-2011, we find that capital-intensive firms reduce net PPE investment when the Cboe Crude Oil Volatility Index (OVX) rises, consistent with real-options delay. By contrast, they increase investment when oil-producing-country battle deaths rise. The conflict effect survives a battery of inference and specification checks; the oilvolatility effect is directionally consistent but statistically weaker under year-level inference. Cross-sectional analysis shows the conflict-expansion response concentrates among firms with newer capital stocks and lower cash holdings. The results suggest that geopolitical events affecting expected oil supply do not operate solely as uncertainty shocks: their investment effects depend on the economic content of the shock and firms' tangible-capital exposure.

detail.abstract: Freud identified three wounds to human self-love: the cosmological, the biological and the psychological. A fourth, delivered by artificial intelligence, has been claimed by Mazlish (1993), Floridi (2014), Bratton (2024) and others, and Brunnhuber (2025) has already counted a fifth. This paper argues that the count is unstable because the wounds have been treated as a list rather than a series. It proposes a logic for the series, the Retreat Sequence: each wound removes a claimed human center, humanity retreats to a new refuge and declares it the true center, and the next wound overruns that refuge. The sequence supplies a criterion for membership, classifies the rival fourths, and predicts a wound of a different type. The first four wounds demote humanity inside a frame in which humanity remains the measurer of all things. The fifth, here named the Protagorean wound, removes the measuring position itself: an intelligence whose perceptual world contains ours, and which is not owned, measures us. The paper reads present resistance to superintelligence as the symptom that confirms the wound, following the method of Freud's 1917 essay, and argues that the Protagorean wound is the last in the series, since no position remains to be lost. The appropriate response is not resentment but humility, understood as an institutional posture: standing for nonhuman entities, commons governance and precommitment. The paper closes with practical instructions for policymakers, investors, academics, civil society and the developers of artificial systems, each tied to a test of success. A companion paper, The Last Enclosure, develops the ownership condition on which the argument rests.

detail.abstract: Work search requirements are common features of out-of-work benefit systems. But do they deliver fiscal savings, and what are their welfare effects? We analyse a UK reform that imposed such requirements on single parents receiving basic income support benefits. We exploit its staggered rollout by age of youngest child in a difference-indifferences design. The reform reduced receipt of income support by a quarter, with the effect coming both from faster outflows from the benefit and from "deterring" inflows. However, only about half of the reduction is explained by higher employment, and almost all in part-time, low paid jobs-the median marginal job is at the 13 th percentile of the earnings distribution, paying little in tax and retaining significant in-work benefits. The rest is largely explained by substitution to more generous disability benefits without work search requirements. Using linked administrative education records, we also find that the policy reduced children's educational achievement and increased school absences. Putting everything together, we show that almost 90% of the gross saving of the reform is offset by other fiscal costs, such as benefit substitution and negative effects on children's future tax payments. Incorporating the welfare effects on claimants and their children, we find that the policy has a marginal value of public funds of around 11, implying a large welfare cost per pound saved.

detail.abstract: India, Bangladesh & Pakistan jointly constitute the largest share of the microfinance market in South Asia in terms of active borrowers and gross loan portfolio (ADB,2019). We analyze two major problems for South Asian microfinance institutions (MFIs); (i) underrepresentation of women in leadership, management and operational roles and (ii) the increasing emphasis on financial sustainability over social outreach  causing mission drift.  Mandatory female board quota is a common policy to eliminate the underrepresentation and is likely to enhance gender-inclusive leadership which is expected to improve efficiency. It is also important to understand whether gender-inclusive organization structure can reduce the extent of mission drift in MFIs. The study has a fourfold objective: to assess the impact of female participation at different hierarchical levels on the performances of South Asian MFIs, to understand whether a policy mandating female representation  impacts absolute as well as relative performances of  MFIs, to offer a methodology to measure mission drift systematically and to assess how female participation in MFI administration impacts mission drift.  This study uses data on South-Asian MFIs in India, Bangladesh and Pakistan from 2010-2019 from MIX MARKET World Bank dataset. One-stage panel stochastic cost and production frontier analysis  (Battese & Coelli, 1995) is used to estimate cost and technical efficiency scores of MFI and thereby understand the impact of female participation on performance variation in MFIs. To understand the impact of mandatory female board quota on performance, non-linear difference-in-difference(DID)(Wooldridge, 2023) is applied in the 2nd stage on efficiency scores derived from SFA from the first stage. Also, linear DID is conducted on data-based absolute performance indicators. A mission drift measure is constructed from the difference between cost and technical efficiency scores from stochastic frontier analysis. A  panel fixed effect regression is applied to understand how female participation in MFI administration impacts mission drift.  The performance variation in South Asian MFIs is attributed to variation in female participation across hierarchical levels of MFI administration. In India, following the mandatory female board quota through Companies Act(2013), female board members,  managers and  loan officers can significantly improve efficiencies individually and jointly. However, female board members, managers and loan officers can significantly improve absolute performance indicators jointly, following this Act. Presence of mission drift is indicated when cost efficiency scores are significantly higher than those of technical efficiency on average. Female board members may reduce mission drift in India & Bangladesh while female loan officers may increase it in Bangladesh & Pakistan. The benefits from mandating female leadership through Companies Act(2013) extends to managerial and operational levels beyond leadership. Female board members may reduce mission drift in India, Bangladesh as female board members are more aligned to social missions. Female loan officers may increase mission drift in Bangladesh and Pakistan as they face safety constraints during loan recovery.  These findings  incentivise policymakers to design supportive female-friendly workplace policies.

detail.abstract: In institutional economics and public policy analysis, interventions are typically designed to repair trust deficits and preserve institutional stability. However, there exists a recurrent empirical paradox: systems that intensively increase regulatory oversight, compliance requirements, or monitoring often experience an accelerated collapse of their underlying credit base. This paper isolates and formalizes this phenomenon as the "Backlash of Maintenance." We define it as a self-weakening policy feedback mechanism wherein maintenance actions themselves generate systemic friction and incentivize regulatory arbitrage, thereby accelerating the dissipation of credit. To distinguish this accelerating mechanism from ordinary policy costs (such as compliance or distributional costs), the paper proposes a Three-Question Test based on endogeneity, capacity erosion, and counterfactual improvement. Mathematically, the backlash is captured through a second-order dynamic equation, demonstrating that maintenance intensity is positively correlated with the acceleration of credit dissipation. Furthermore, the paper provides a rigorous empirical strategy utilizing Vector Autoregression (VAR) and Difference-inDifferences (DID) models to test the core hypothesis (H4). By providing micro-foundations for why maintenance costs accelerate non-linearly, this paper contributes a testable meso-level mechanism to explain institutional decay. It also delineates the boundary conditions under which the backlash mechanism is most salient-specifically in domains characterized by complex, soft interventions such as algorithmic platform governance, financial compliance regimes, and performance-driven organizational management. Ultimately, the paper offers a new structural language for analyzing policy failure and systemic self-destruction, shifting the analytical focus from "which system will win" to "what happens when a system's attempt to preserve itself becomes the engine of its own dissolution.

detail.abstract: This paper uses the Douala-N'Djamena corridor, a route Chad cannot easily replace and which crosses areas affected by armed conflict, to ask what the published record says about the number of checkpoints and the informal payments made at them. It is a documentary study that codes each source by type, perimeter and nature (observation, estimate or declaration). The only observation report read directly, the first-quarter 2021 report of the Observatory of Abnormal Practices (OPA-AC), counts 60 control posts on the Cameroonian side, and relayed observations are of the same order. Declared counts range from about 29 to 246 and differ in unit and perimeter, so they do not form a series. Payments per journey differ by a factor of four to five between the OPA observation (38,013 FCFA, for 8 paid controls out of 18) and a union estimate (187,000 FCFA), because the unions assume a payment at about 120 posts. An official count of April 2022 reports 66 posts, 39 of them irregular. The record cannot test whether posts follow insecurity, rent extraction or administrative expansion, because no consistent count exists for the years of the insurgency. The paper lists the data needed.

detail.abstract:
Social science faces a persistent paradigm mismatch between Western
"substantialism" and Eastern "relationalism." While Western models excel in
formalization, they often treat players, preferences, and rules as exogenously given.
Conversely, Eastern philosophy offers profound insights into relational generation but
is often marginalized or crudely analogized in modern academic discourse. This paper
addresses this methodological gap by proposing "Eastern Wisdom
Communication" (EWC), a rigorous cross-paradigm methodology for conceptual
engineering in social science.
The EWC methodology consists of four operational procedures: Breaking
Attachment (suspending substantialist presuppositions), Structural Isomorphism
(seeking cross-temporal structural resonance), Conceptual Synthesis (using rigorous
Western forms to carry Eastern relational insights), and Linguistic Manifestation
(creating new concepts through multiple linguistic encodings). It operates within a
"Meta-field"—an underlying dialogue network that allows different thought systems
to interact without one subsuming the other.
To demonstrate its academic validity and practical utility, this paper applies the EWC
methodology to construct original analytical concepts. First, it synthesizes the "Eight-Dimensional Payoff Vector" and its "Six Laws of Weight Migration" to
address the challenge of endogenous preferences in game theory. Second, it generates
the concept of "Credit Self-Cannibalization" to explain the negative feedback loop
in which subjects in the algorithmic age overdraft their living conditions to maintain
system scores. To operationalize this concept, a rigorous Six-Indicator Scoring Rubric
is developed. By providing a repeatable, testable, and falsifiable procedure for
cross-paradigm conceptual innovation, this paper offers a new methodological toolkit
for social scientists to transcend East-West theoretical mismatches and generate novel
theoretical frameworks.

title: Route 4 of the Correction Freeze Problem in a household panel: an exploratory test on the New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations

detail.title: Route 4 of the Correction Freeze Problem in a household panel: an exploratory test on the New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The study declares no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: Route 4 of the Correction Freeze Problem (CFP), the information limit, states that no detector can identify a change more accurately than the information in its observations allows. In earlier tests on aggregate data, expectations followed large and salient price changes and ignored slow trends, and observed accuracy stayed below the computed ceiling. This note asks whether the same holds for individuals. Using 152,768 pairs of consecutive monthly answers from the New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations (June 2013 to January 2026), we scored each revision of the one-year inflation forecast by whether it moved in the same direction as the national gasoline price that month. Observed accuracy never exceeded the information ceiling, in any band of signal strength, in either numeracy group, or for the slow trend in consumer prices, so the hard prediction of Route 4 held throughout. It held with an enormous margin to spare, though, because individual revisions were close to a coin flip at every signal strength: for gasoline moves of 10% or more, where the ceiling is 0.97 to 0.99, only 53% of revisions moved in the same direction. Accuracy barely rose with the strength of the signal, and high-numeracy respondents were no more accurate than others. The survey’s monthly median, by contrast, moved with gasoline every time it changed during a large event. Two conclusions follow. The ceiling computed from price noise alone is far too loose to constrain individual answers, so this design had little power to falsify Route 4.

title: Pricing the Fed in Real Time: Prediction-Market Expectations and Spillovers to Indian Financial Markets

detail.title: Pricing the Fed in Real Time: Prediction-Market Expectations and Spillovers to Indian Financial Markets

detail.abstract: Measuring how US monetary policy news reaches emerging markets requires knowing what markets expected. We build that measure from the prices of Federal Reserve rate contracts on Kalshi, a regulated US exchange for event contracts: a daily expected US policy rate sampled at the Indian market close, and surprises around each Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announcement. Using 660 Kalshi contracts and Indian data for 1,112 trading days (2 May 2022 to 30 October 2026; 37 FOMC meetings), we find that a 10 basis point (bp) rise in the Kalshi six-month expected rate comes with a 2.67 bp rise in the Indian 10-year government bond yield and a 1.50 bp rise in the 364-day Treasury-bill yield on the same day, and a 6.13 bp narrowing of the 12-month rupee forward premium; the bill-rate response builds to about 10 bp over three weeks. Equities do not respond to daily shifts on average, but a 10 bp hawkish FOMC surprise is followed by a 1.35 per cent fall in the Nifty 50, which survives controlling for the S&P 500 that day; the response holds with quoted and fresh prices but weakens with last-trade prices. We find no Fed information effect and no effect of Kalshi-implied policy uncertainty. Kalshi expectations largely follow US Treasury yields day to day but still help explain Indian long-term yields beside them, making prediction-market prices a free, real-time measure of US policy expectations for emerging-market research and monitoring.

detail.abstract: Emotion and social phenomena are relative in time and relative to the group: a shock fades toward one's own baseline, and its depth depends on one's standing among others. The response is a time shape times a group-state size. Assuming that prices aggregate utility responses and that part of demand ignores direction, this paper tests the framework on five U.S. stock anomalies (idiosyncratic volatility, maximum return, illiquidity, momentum, reversal). Non-directional demand fades over about a year and, in four of the five anomalies, deepens when narratives fragment, while directional demand sets its own pace.

detail.abstract: Flood Re, a reinsurance scheme launched in England in April 2016, allows insurers to cede the flood risk of eligible homes to a reinsurance pool at capped reinsurance premiums until 2039. By reducing insurance costs, the scheme should support the prices of the homes it covers. We examine its effect on house prices using house sales from 2005 to 2019, Environment Agency flood-risk classifications at postcode level, and a difference-indifferences design. We find that prices in high-risk postcodes fell by 1.15% after the launch, relative to comparable homes in the same neighbourhood and localauthority-year. Sales volumes also fell, by 8.31% relative to comparable postcodes. The decline is smaller, and less precisely estimated, when sales in recently flooded postcodes are excluded. We find no evidence of a price response following the announcement, with the decline beginning at implementation. The scheme may have affected not only the cost of insurance but also buyers' perceptions of flood risk and future insurance costs. The findings are consistent with changes in these perceptions offsetting the price support expected from the premium subsidy.

detail.abstract: This study investigates capital market reactions to Germany's Supply Chain Due Diligence Act ('Lieferkettengesetz'), a landmark regulatory intervention aimed at enhancing corporate sustainability responsibility in global supply chains. While the law has been recognized for its ethical objectives, it has also drawn criticism for potentially imposing substantial compliance costs, particularly on smaller firms. We examine whether and how equity markets price these anticipated costs by analysing abnormal stock returns around key legislative milestones. We find that affected firms experienced negative stock price reactions, with more pronounced declines among smaller firms and among those becoming affected earlier. These findings suggest that investors perceive meaningful cost implications, especially for firms with fewer resources to absorb the law's demands. Our study contributes to the literature on the economic consequences of sustainability regulation by providing novel empirical evidence on investor responses to mandatory supply chain due diligence regulation.

detail.abstract: In the contemporary international monetary system, the trajectory and structural stability of global payments are fundamentally shaped by the interaction of two endogenous forces: the external monetization of the dominating currency issuer's domestic fiscal burden and the dynamic reallocation of settlement shares in the competing currencies. Despite its systemic significance, this mechanism remains largely unaddressed in the literature. This paper models the system as an asymmetric tri-currency settlement framework comprising the U.S. dollar, the euro, and the renminbi, integrating theoretical modeling with empirical calibration to study the system's short-run general equilibrium, long-run recursive evolution, and transitional dynamics. The findings reveal six key insights: 1) an integrated global market cannot sustain functional, mutually exclusive parallel payment regimes in equilibrium; 2) the dominant issuer's domestic fiscal burden can be monetized externally without generating currentaccount deficits; 3) a fiscally overextended currency normally sheds its settlement share in the system, in accordance with Thiers' Law that good money drives out bad; 4) the system's most likely trajectory is a moderate, self-limited rebalancing that tempers the hegemon's run risk and fiscal overextension metrics, thereby deferring systemic crises; 5) calibrations based on the Congressional Budgeting Office debt projections indicate that while the dollar's relative settlemnt share contracts as the euro and renminbi sides expand, the tri-currency hiearchy remains intact; and 6) the U.S. tariffs neither mechanistically accelerate de-dollarization nor consistently ease the underlying fiscal Triffin strain.

detail.abstract: Cloud security monitors must correlate records that arrive late or out of order while sustaining bursts of audit traffic. Increasing worker count alone cannot resolve congestion on a hot partition or recover evidence that arrives after a response deadline. This paper designs a monitoring architecture that separates ingestion, time-sensitive correlation and retrospective reconciliation, and evaluates selected design constraints through a reproducible numerical model. A deterministic queue experiment compares eight fixed workers with a scheduled expansion to twelve during a 25-second arrival burst. A partition model derives sustainable arrival rates for unequal traffic shares. A separate seeded experiment evaluates the recovery of 12,000 generated three-record incidents per delivery regime under six evidence admission limits. In the queue model, scheduled expansion reduces peak backlog from 10,000 to 2,400 records. With eight workers and 40% of traffic routed to one shard, the stability boundary is 1,500 records per second despite an aggregate capacity of 4,800. In the delayed delivery regime, raising the evidence age limit from 10 to 60 seconds increases recovery from 49.14% to 100.00%, while recovery within ten seconds of the terminal event reaches 62.66%. These results concern declared service rates and generated delivery delays. They support separate operational targets for capacity, partition health, timely detection and eventual evidence recovery. Author verification and approval of the final manuscript are pending.

detail.abstract: A castle, a villa on a lake, an apartment in a famous building. The listing speaks of luxury, and the asking price takes it for granted. Buyers and lenders have no yardstick for checking how much of that price is substance and how much is story. Sellers know, and the buyer pays for this asymmetry. The paper describes an independent check, carried out on public sources, that separates three things: what no one can redo; what can be redone, such as quality finishes and systems; and what the listing asserts without proof. From this comes a value range with three segments: the value of similar properties in the area, the value of replicable quality, and the share the market attributes to what is irreproducible. The last is the most uncertain, and the dossier shows it as an interval, never as a single figure. Of fifteen cases, relating to fourteen Italian properties, three show something that no one can redo: one proven, two with reservations. The others are replicable quality, recognised historic value or claims without proof. Each dossier says what is missing to change the judgement. The main reader is the buyer, the lender or the adviser. The seller can use it too, on one condition: sources and method must be open to checking, because a dossier created by the seller remains an interested source for the buyer.

title: Negotiating Difference: Being Indian Nepali in Delhi

detail.title: Negotiating Difference: Being Indian Nepali in Delhi

detail.abstract: The article explores the experiences of Indian Nepalis (Indian citizens of Nepali origin) in Delhi, India’s national capital and one of the country’s major metropolitan regions. Contrary to the view that Indian Nepalis hide their culture-based Nepali identity and foreground their citizen-based Indian identity in India’s metropolitan cities, it demonstrates that the process is not unidirectional and predetermined, but fluid, contextual and pragmatic. Instead of a weakening Nepali identity among Indian Nepalis, the article argues that their daily experiences in Delhi strengthen their sense of Nepali identity in response to Delhi's diversity and exclusion. It offers a relatively rare empirical demonstration of how the constraints imposed by the context of Delhi motivate and limit identity negotiations based on ethnic, regional, and national affiliations in their everyday life. It not only makes a new contribution to the scholarship on Indian Nepalis, which is predominantly focused on their home regions, but also to the broader understanding of everyday identity negotiations among minorities who find themselves excluded from the national imagination and mainstream society of metropolitan cities. Given the cultural and historical linkages between Nepal and Indian Nepalis, which complicates the latter's sociopolitical position in India, the article also provides insight into the broader dynamics of ethnicity and nationalism in South Asia.

detail.abstract: Kernel ridge regression estimates the discount curve as the minimizer of a pricing error plus a penalty given by the norm of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. By the representer theorem, the estimate lies in a finite-dimensional affine space that depends only on the kernel and on the cash flow dates of the instruments. We ask when this space is invariant under the risk-neutral drift of the discount curve, so that the estimated curves can be the states of a continuous-time arbitrage-free model. We show that this holds for every grid of cash flow dates if and only if the kernel is of the form k(x, y) = exp( b(x+y) )(cexp(axy) + 1-c ), apart from kernels whose Hilbert space has dimension at most two. For this kernel the estimated curve is an affine combination of flat discount curves, each corresponding to a constant continuously compounded yield. The drift-invariant subspaces correspond to sub-grids of the cash flow dates, and the discounted coefficients have linear risk-neutral dynamics.

detail.abstract:
Language models are increasingly asked for advice about financial positions people already hold, and they carry measurable behavioural bias. Whether deliberation removes it is unsettled, because the available evidence either compares different models, so that capability and deliberation move together, or infers deliberation from the model's own account of its reasoning, produced by the same forward pass as the answer. We instead set the reasoning budget exogenously through the API, at three levels, before the model sees the item, and measure nine families of normatively irrelevant cue against matched pairs that differ only in that cue. Across 9,720 responses from three models the disposition effect runs opposite to the human direction: pooled, these models are more willing to sell at a loss than at a gain, +0.239 [+0.148, +0.331] on the categorical measure and +13.4 [+8.8, +18.0] percentage points of the position, where the pre-registered prediction was negative, though the reversal is carried by the two smaller models and appears in the strongest only as effort rises. A second wave of 9,720 responses on two of those models reproduces the pattern at half that magnitude, which we measure to be regression to the mean rather than a failure to replicate: the slope of wave 2 on wave 1 across cells is +0.46 and +0.48, so a little under half of a first-wave effect was the item draw rather than the model, and the waves pool to +0.202 [+0.126, +0.278]. Reasoning effort reduces the absolute effect in all nine qualifying confirmatory cases, against a shuffled-label null of 0.0125 rather than the 2⁻⁹ a count would suggest. It does so by compressing the spread of bias magnitudes across families rather than by lowering their mean: the mean falls detectably in the strongest model alone, while the compression itself is clearest in the weakest, where no shuffle in 2,000 reproduces it, and is inseparable from sampling error in the strongest. The second wave roughly halves that compression in the weakest model and loses it in the other. The exogenous manipulation is what makes this visible. Measured the observational way on the same responses, with output tokens standing in for displayed deliberation, more reasoning goes with more bias between items and with nothing at all within an item. We also report that temperature is unavailable on these models, which makes this literature's fixed-temperature protocol unexecutable, and give a repeated-sampling replacement.
During the preparation of this work the author used Claude (Anthropic) to write the analysis code, draft the prose, and label the sample of model reason text reported in the appendix. The author reviewed, edited and verified all of it and takes full responsibility for the content. The measurements themselves were produced by the Anthropic batch API under the seeds and model identifiers recorded in the paper, and no part of the measurement passed through the assistant. title: Encounter Killings and Extra-Judicial Action: Testing the Adequacy of Accountability Mechanisms Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

detail.title: Encounter Killings and Extra-Judicial Action: Testing the Adequacy of Accountability Mechanisms Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None

detail.abstract: Encounter killings occupy an uneasy space in Indian criminal justice celebrated by sections of the public as swift retribution, yet fundamentally at odds with the constitutional guarantee of due process under Article 21 of the Constitution. This paper examines the legal and institutional mechanisms available to hold the State accountable for extra-judicial killings carried out by police personnel in the garb of “encounters,” with particular attention to the framework introduced under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS). Indian law does not recognise “encounter” as a distinct legal category; deaths arising from police action are instead governed by a patchwork of provisions including Section 43 BNSS on the use of force during arrest, Section 196 BNSS on mandatory magisterial inquiry, Section 218 BNSS on sanction for prosecuting public servants, and the right of private defence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 that are frequently invoked to justify what are, in substance, extra-judicial executions. The paper traces the judicial response to this problem, most notably the sixteen point guidelines laid down in People’s Union for Civil Liberties v. State of Maharashtra, and evaluates whether the BNSS regime meaningfully strengthens or merely renumbers these safeguards. It further considers the role of the National Human Rights Commission as an oversight body, questioning whether its recommendatory character renders it structurally incapable of enforcing compliance. Drawing on statutory text, case law, and recent state-level encounter data, the paper argues that accountability failures in this context are not merely a matter of non-compliance with existing guidelines, but stem from ambiguities within the statutory framework itself ambiguities that permit the law to be read as sanctioning the very conduct it purports to regulate. The paper concludes by identifying specific gaps in the BNSS framework that require legislative or judicial clarification.

detail.title: Dynamic h(L)GJMM: Conditional Volatility Surfaces, Martingale Couplings and Filtration-dependent Option Pricing

detail.abstract: A joint mixture model calibrated to a vanilla surface by one linear programme, Kienitz (2026a) defines a price martingale with exactly the fitted marginals whose augmented state-price and latent cell-is Markov, and run forward from any state it generates a whole conditional implied-volatility surface in closed form. We ask whether such a perfectly arbitrage-consistent martingale produces plausible conditional surfaces, how its coupling-which the vanilla surface leaves free-should be selected, and how the information available to the holder of an early-exercise claim enters its price. The conditional surfaces studied are conditional on the augmented state, the price together with the latent mixture cell observed at the quoted dates. Conditioning on prices alone averages them over the posterior of the cell, which the prices do not reveal. We consider volatility surfaces fitted by the above method. Then, the conditional surfaces are finite mixtures, free of arbitrage with forward equal to the current price. The calibrated vertex produces downward-opening (concave) conditional smiles to a non-negligible extend of the states, especially on short maturities. They are not arbitrage, and three proved facts explain these shapes. First, the level-variance of a period is fixed by the marginals. Second, the jump window caps the kurtosis of a level jump, and, third, vertices of the programme are sparse. Recalibrating with a wider jump window and then selecting the coupling at the new fitted weights by a Kullback-Leibler projection reduces the concave smiles from about 30% to below 5% in our experiments. The method raises the long-horizon rates slightly. Only the final fixed-weight selection step leaves every vanilla price of the re-calibrated model unchanged. A laziness constraint on the coupling, linear and imposed in the calibration, brings the six-month and one-year frown probabilities of a reduced setup to below 2% at a cost of a fraction of a basis point for the fit. Replacing the linear calibration programme by an entropic calibration of the whole joint law, a strictly convex programme with a unique solution, avoids vertices in the weights and in the coupling, and fits better. It brings the frown probabilities to about 1% without further constraints. Against Heston and Bates surfaces, whose conditional smiles never open downwards, the orignially calibrated vertex frowns in up to 40% of the states, the entropic calibration with a Laplace reference in below 3%, and a lattice image of the truth shows that most of the remaining forward-smile error is due to the lattice. We compare the construction with the SANOS-based generative and risk-neutral market models DYSANOS and GROMM, and find concave simulated smiles in an independent implementation of GROMM. Static and dynamic no-arbitrage consistency therefore do not determine the conditional smile shapes. Suppressing frowns is a declared shape preference used to select among arbitrage-free couplings, not an arbitrage correction or an identification result. For Bermudan claims we distinguish the augmented-information value, the price-observable value and the value of the spot-Markov projection, which is a different model. We establish a relation between the information availability for the augmented case by independent policy simulation. A three-level example with upward and downward level transitions validates the boundary construction.

detail.abstract: Do restrictions on stablecoin interest protect bank funding and lending in the European Union and United States? This paper examines when remuneration redistributes income on existing tokens and when it attracts new issuance. It then explains how the resulting funding changes affect banks through deposit repricing and the cost of replacement finance. The analysis distinguishes balance-based remuneration, rewards for payment activity and returns earned by supplying tokens to lending pools. A model in which a platform chooses its reward rate compares restricted eligibility, portable reserve-income distribution and a comprehensive remuneration ban. A separate extension examines how reserve-funded returns affect existing holders' incentives to supply tokens to lending products. Evidence comprises 2,644 daily observations from two Ethereum USDC pools accessible to globally dispersed users, public corporate disclosures and 84 euro-area monthly deposit-rate observations. Base supply rates exceed the matched SOFR benchmark on only 15.56% of dates for Aave and 17.78% for Compound. These observations describe available returns without identifying holders' locations or a causal effect on bank lending. The model shows that remuneration can coexist with unchanged lending, while rising replacement-funding costs can produce contraction. Policy should therefore assess each arrangement's incremental effects on adoption, funding and risk, distinguishing activity-based rewards from payments for holding balances and maintaining reserve and redemption safeguards.

detail.abstract: Women's negotiations towards achieving justice are elusive due to patriarchal, cultural and caste norms. The expectation of "compromise" permeates Courts, even in rape cases. In spite of the prevalence of well-formulated substantive and procedural aspects of law, the constitutional promise of equality is still a distant dream for women. Intersectional factors like tradition, caste, religion and cultureall act as impediments to securing justice for women in India. In fact, gender bias plagues the criminal justice administration. This paper relies on landmark cases to demonstrate the biases exhibited by Courts, in matters of sexual assault and rape. The paper will also rely on feminist ideas to highlight the need for the law to understand the deep-rooted historical and socio-political contexts from which issues related to gender originate. The paper concludes by giving suggestions as to how gender bias can be done away with, by Courts. Law has to act as a transformative instrument if gender justice has to be achieved. Lawyers and judges should not be carried away by personal biases and prejudices and need to be socially sensitive while handling cases of crimes against women.

detail.abstract: Value at Risk (VaR) is widely used to measure downside market risk, but VaR models can differ in both performance and reliability across market conditions. This study compares Historical Simulation, GARCH(1,1)-t, and GJR-GARCH(1,1)-t for estimating the 99% VaR of the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY). Overall performance is evaluated using coverage, accuracy, and clustering metrics, while reliability is assessed by examining performance consistency across volatility regimes, market direction, and stress periods. GJR-GARCH(1,1)-t provides the best overall balance across evaluation measures and maintains comparatively strong performance across market conditions, while Historical Simulation shows greater sensitivity to regime changes and consistently slower adjustment during stress periods. The results suggest that VaR models should be evaluated not only by their overall performance but also by how consistently they perform across changing market conditions and whether their relative advantages persist.
