detail.abstract: In financial time series, a level shift (also known as a jump) is a prominent feature influencing the dynamics of a series. Despite this, the widely adopted bubble regime change point estimation literature typically omits this aspect, and when accounted for, it adversely affects the accuracy of existing estimators. Therefore, we present two primary contributions: (1) we demonstrate how level shifts impact the accuracy of the Harvey et al. (2017) and Pang et al. (2021) procedures, which have been established as a more precise bubble regime change point estimator than the Phillips et al. (2015) procedure, conditioning only one bubble is present in the series; and (2) we propose new estimators robust to both level shifts and time varying volatility. The performance of the proposed estimator is evaluated using large sample theory, finite sample simulations, and an empirical application to NASDAQ 100 data covering the Dot-com bubble period. Our findings from finite-sample simulations demonstrate that, when level shifts and time varying volatility are sizeable, our estimator generally outperforms existing methods. In the application, our procedure identifies regime change dates at more intuitively reasonable points compared to the other estimators.

title: Beyond SABR: The Differential Geometry of ZABR, Mean-Reverting SABR and Free SABR With a Financial Dictionary of the Geometric Quantities

detail.title: Beyond SABR: The Differential Geometry of ZABR, Mean-Reverting SABR and Free SABR With a Financial Dictionary of the Geometric Quantities

detail.abstract: SABR lives on the Poincaré half-plane, and several coupled SABR models live on a solvable Lie group with a left-invariant metric. This note determines which of those statements hold for three neighbours of SABR. For ZABR, whose volatility is a CEV process with exponent γ, the plane becomes a warped product whose curvature depends on the volatility level and is exactly flat at γ = 2. The Lie group is lost, but the metric keeps constant coefficients in the same coframe. Hence the normal form, the gauge nature of the backbone correlations and the closed-form curvatures carry over with one explicit correction, and the strike distance becomes one scalar equation with incomplete-Beta integrals. For γ > 1 the point of infinite volatility is at finite distance, which caps every strike distance. For mean-reverting SABR the geometry and, at regular interior feet, the leading-order smile are unchanged; mean reversion enters at order T through a drift one-form with an explicit curl. For free SABR the state space is the complete hyperbolic plane; we characterise when the minimising geodesic to a positive strike stays positive, and we prove the logarithmic rate of the probability of hitting zero (the mass at zero in the absorbing model) for every correlation. Theorems carry their hypotheses and proofs. Monte-Carlo and quadrature results are labelled as numerical and hold for the stated parameter sets.

title: Price-Volume Correlations Are Always Zero

detail.title: Price-Volume Correlations Are Always Zero

detail.abstract: We argue that the use of the empirical time series of values, volumes, and prices of consecutive trades made during the averaging interval to calculate the price-volume correlation in a way that follows the definition of correlation always gives zero correlation. We show that the usual expression for the empirical calculation of the correlation misleads the researchers and doesn't fulfill the definition of price-volume correlation. The mistake has its origin in the dependence of volume weighted average price on the mean values and volumes of trades during the averaging interval but not on time series of prices only. The true sense of the declared positive or negative results of the empirical calculations of price-volume correlations made by numerous researchers in reality is determined by the difference between the volume weighted average price and its limiting expression of average price, which is correct only when all volumes of consecutive trades are constant, and multiplication of this difference by the mean trade volume. To empirically determine the statistical dependence between time series of prices and trade volumes, one should calculate the correlations between prices and squares of trade volumes or correlations between squares of prices and squares of volumes. We derive the expressions for empirical calculations of these correlations.

detail.abstract: Using a high-frequency identification approach, we establish stock prices don't fully incorporate biased information. We study the announcements of easily quantifiable value-relevant news during voluntary corporate disclosure events where bias has been widely documented. For a large cross-section, we observe that market prices move in the same direction when the manager communicates cash-flow projections and when the same estimates are repeated by analysts the day after. Our findings are consistent with models in which investors have a heterogeneous interpretation of managerial announcements due to unknown reporting bias. We discuss alternative explanations and the implications of our results for market efficiency.

detail.abstract: The official Indian statistical systems produce significant numbers of statistics relating to religious minorities, but some indicators of socioeconomic and security outcomes of Muslims are collected inconsistently, selectively excluded, or abandoned after being published. This creates a type of non-random missingness which is not explicitly recorded or taken into account in analyses done downstream of these data sources, but is considered as anomalies that are unique to a specific domain in the literature instead of systematic design failure or revision of the official data infrastructure. This research fills this gap by conducting a comparative document audit on major Indian statistical publications over the years covering 2006-2024, namely Census, SECC, NCRB Crime in India, NCRB Prison Statistics, and administrative personnel records. It creates and uses a four-part classification of data that are not enumerated, collected but were not published, discontinued after publication, or reclassified into nonidentifying data. It codes the presence of variables by publication year to generate a comparative timeline of availability of each of the four categories of data by domain. The approach is explained in the case of the Prison Statistics series published by NCRB, which included a discontinuity in the process of gathering data on religion/caste of prisoners, as while data was published on religion/caste of prisoners every year till 2015, it was missing in 2016-17 and was published again without change in 2018, which was a period of communal tensions in the country. The study's methodological contribution is that a replicable framework for auditing non-random data absence in official statistics can be applied in other cases than the one studied, which could be any population that is subject to selective statistical visibility.

detail.abstract: This paper specifies the S0/S1/S2 stablecoin monetary aggregates, a three-tier classification of fiat-denominated stablecoin claims expressed in United States dollars at official reference exchange rates. The tiers are ordered by claim form: primary claims, representations of those claims in other settlement environments, and other transferable claims derived from them. For each admitted instrument, the specification also records claim distance, defined as the number of redemption steps between the token held and the base instrument's redemption endpoint. That endpoint may be an issuer redemption obligation or a protocol redemption mechanism. S0 measures base stablecoin supply: native primary stablecoin claims intended to redeem at or track par. S1 measures represented supply by adding tokenized representations of S0 claims created in other settlement environments. S2 measures extended claims by adding transferable instruments whose principal exposure can be traced to an S0 asset. S1 and S2 are each defined on a net basis, which deduplicates backing relationships, and a gross basis, which counts every token layer circulating at the same time. The ratio of gross extended claims to base supply, termed the representation multiplier, measures the amount of claim structure built on each unit of base supply. The specification defines the equations, constituent admission policy, and edge-case rules for bridge designs, wrapper chains, tranches, rebasing designs, issuer treasury balances, tokenized securities, and claims issued in excess of backing held. It also establishes the versioning and revisions policy. The aggregates are published as a maintained daily series.

detail.abstract: Critical-link analysis often relies on compact indicators or reduced candidate sets to avoid repeated post-failure evaluation, but such reductions do not necessarily preserve the critical-link decision as O-D demand changes. This study examines what information is required for exact critical-link identification and when that information can be reduced without altering the decision. Link-failure consequence is measured by the demand-weighted increase in O-D shortest-path cost after removal of a physical link. We show that rich descriptions of the intact network do not guarantee recovery of the post-failure ranking. Specifically, we construct an infinite family of planar, cubic, and 3-vertex-connected graph pairs with identical spectra under four standard graph matrices but different worst-link consequences. Adding O-D demand and baseline flow provides more information about network use, but does not ensure recovery of the post-failure ordering. We then represent post-failure information through a failure-response operator. When admissible O-D demand lies within a structured demand space, the exact failure response can be constructed from a basis for that space without forming the full edge-by-O-D matrix. The reduced response preserves all link consequences, rankings, critical-link sets, and switching boundaries. It also enables exact removal of links that cannot become critical anywhere in that demand space. The candidate set is reduced from 38 links to 2 in Sioux Falls and from 1,071 non-bridge links to 5 in Chicago-Sketch. The framework provides an exact basis for repeated critical-link analysis as O-D conditions change.

title: Advertising Activity as an Alternative Data Signal for Equity Investing

detail.title: Advertising Activity as an Alternative Data Signal for Equity Investing

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors are affiliated with Brain. Oxford Data Plan commissioned and funded this study, which evaluates its Advertiser Insights dataset. Brain was responsible for conducting the research, including the methodology, analysis, and conclusions presented. Brain conducted the research independently and objectively, maintaining full scientific autonomy over the methodology, analytical approach, interpretation of results, and conclusions.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was commissioned and funded by Oxford Data Plan and conducted by Brain.

detail.abstract:
The Oxford Data Plan Advertiser Insights dataset provides weekly modelled estimates of digital advertising spend. These estimates are derived from advertising impressions observed through a U.S.-centric panel of consented users, with spend estimated using cost per thousand impressions (CPM) models. Brain maps the resulting advertiser-, brand-, and platform-level estimates to public companies and constructs company-level features for quantitative analysis.

After documenting data coverage, public-equity mapping, and key dataset characteristics, we construct advertising-derived features designed to capture multiple dimensions of advertising behavior, including spending levels, advertising intensity, consecutive and year-over-year growth, acceleration, surprise, momentum, active brands, active platforms, and sector-normalized behavior.

These features are integrated into Brain's internal cross-sectional ranking-validation framework and evaluated across the U.S., Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Global investment universes. Historical correlations with forward stock returns are measured using quintile portfolio tests, Information Coefficients, and temporal stability analyses, while factor-exposure diagnostics are used to characterize the relationship between the advertising-derived features and established equity risk factors. Finally, we provide an illustrative example of constructing an adaptive composite advertising signal, in which features are dynamically selected out of sample based on their historical cross-sectional Information Coefficients and combined into a single ranking signal.

This study provides results from a point-in-time quantitative analysis of advertising-derived variables, together with an extensive examination of the dataset. Overall, the analysis suggests that advertising-derived variables represent an interesting source of alternative-data features for quantitative research and may be used individually or combined into composite signals, subject to further validation before any live investment application.

Given the number of evaluated features, the analysis cannot fully rule out selection bias or establish that the measured historical correlations will persist in the future. To mitigate this point, the study evaluates stability across two distinct time periods and applies an out-of-sample approach in the dynamic feature-selection example.

detail.abstract: This dissertation looks at how the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulates India’s primary market. It uses doctrinal analysis of the SEBI Act, 1992, the SCRA, the Depositories Act, the Companies Act, 2013, SEBI’s regulations, case law and committee reports. It covers SEBI’s constitution and powers, the public-issue process under the ICDR Regulations, stock exchanges and depositories, market intermediaries, and corporate governance under the LODR Regulations. The study argues that SEBI’s disclosure-based framework is largely adequate. However, slow enforcement and gaps at the edges of the regulated perimeter limit how well it protects investors. The study suggests reforms in enforcement, gatekeeper accountability, restitution and grievance redress.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how technological disclosures shape financial markets' macroeconomic expectations. I combine semiconductor-sector returns around recurring technology conferences with large language model (LLM) classifications of keynote transcripts. The classification distinguishes technological capability from demand and adoption, and capability already available from capability yet to arrive. I find that positive conference-day surprises are associated with higher economic growth expectations for both delivered-capability-heavy and promised-capability-heavy keynotes, but their inflation implications differ. Expectation is inflationary for delivered-capabilityheavy keynotes and disinflationary for promised-capability-heavy keynotes. These joint responses are consistent with the interplay between anticipated demand expansion and improvements in productive capacity. Subsequent increases in capital-goods orders in both cases, and lower core prices alongside higher production following promised-capability-heavy keynotes, provide complementary evidence. The findings suggest that the economic content of technological disclosures matters for explaining why technology news may have different inflation implications.

detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze accountability and transparency in the development of the Red and White Bridge infrastructure in the Wadas Gumantung area, Kutamendala Village, Tonjong District, Brebes Regency. The infrastructure is important because damage to the previous bridge caused access difficulties for the community, particularly when the water level of the Glagah River increased. This study employs a descriptive qualitative approach using documentary research and literature review methods. Data were obtained from local government publications, relevant agencies, Perhutani, village information portals, and mass media reports containing information on infrastructure planning, implementation, and financing. The findings indicate that in 2019, news reports announced a planned budget of IDR 3 billion for a new bridge, while in 2021, information emerged regarding a proposed relocation involving the use of Perhutani land. In 2024, the bridge was constructed with the involvement of the Indonesian National Armed Forces (TNI), the Indonesian National Police (Polri), local government, residents, and volunteers. In addition, news reports in 2024 announced a planned budget of IDR 2 billion for an approximately two-kilometer access road in 2025. An examination of the Kutamendala Village APBDes portal showed that detailed information on village revenue and expenditure was not available. However, the public sources examined did not provide detailed information on the actual realization of the bridge construction budget, the final land-use agreement, or village financial realization reports specifically related to the project. This study concludes that the physical implementation of the project and the involvement of several parties can be traced through publicly available information, but the traceability of financing and financial accountability remains limited.

detail.abstract: This research examines the advantages and disadvantages of the "fair cost sharing" framework, which authorizes access Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to bill Content Providers (CPs) for a portion of the expenses they generate. Our investigation focuses on an ecosystem where CPs deliver content to users via a platform that employs two-sided pricing mechanisms for mediating between CPs and users. The model is based on a framework where both the ISP and the intermediating platform are complementary platforms between the two sides (users and CPs). We show that an unregulated (two-sided pricing) ISP is harmed by the entry of an (intermediating complementary two-sided pricing) platform, but the ISP has no incentive to claim a regulatory intervention under any rationale, either neutrality, fair cost sharing or full cost recovery. Actually, the claim that the ISPs are then making is not a welfaremaximizing regulation, i.e., fair cost sharing, but either a deregulation, as a firs-best, or a full cost recovery regulation, as a second-best.

detail.abstract:
The patent system is based on a statutory bargain under which an inventor receives exclusive rights in exchange for disclosing the invention to the public in a sufficiently clear and complete manner. In India, Section 10(4) of the Patents Act, 1970, establishes the principal requirements governing the contents of a complete specification, including full and particular description of the invention, its operation or use, the method of performance and disclosure of the best method known to the applicant. 

However, a significant question arises regarding the boundaries of compulsory technical disclosure: Should patent applicants be required to submit component-wise manufacturer datasheets, experimental results, testing procedures and physical working models before filing or during examination of a complete specification? Further, is there a need to introduce a new procedural rule requiring verification of compliance with Section 10(4) before a complete specification is filed? 

This article critically examines the existing Indian patent framework, particularly Sections 10(3), 10(4) and 10(5) of the Patents Act, 1970, and Rules 13 and 16 of the Patents Rules, 2003. It considers the relationship between sufficiency of disclosure, enablement, component-wise technical information, experimental evidence and physical prototypes. It also examines relevant judicial decisions, including Novartis AG v. Union of India and F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd. v. Cipla Ltd., alongside the disclosure principles under Article 29 of TRIPS and Article 5 of the Patent Cooperation Treaty. 

The article argues that the existing legislation already imposes a substantive obligation of sufficient disclosure but lacks a dedicated, standardised pre-filing verification THE NEED FOR PRE-FILING VERIFICATION UNDER SECTION 10(4) OF THE INDIAN PATENTS ACT, 1970 2/15 mechanism addressing the technical completeness of complex inventions. It proposes the introduction of a proportionate Section 10(4) verification framework through Patent Office guidance or an appropriately framed amendment to the Patents Rules. The proposed framework would distinguish essential technical disclosure from supplementary documentation and prevent indiscriminate demands for complete datasheets, experimental records and working models.

title: What Survives Preregistered Testing in Multi-Agent Handoffs?
affiliations: University of Massachusetts Amherst, Georgia Institute of Technology, Duke University and University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign

detail.title: What Survives Preregistered Testing in Multi-Agent Handoffs?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Genliang Zhu and Chu Wang are affiliated with Accentrust, as stated in the manuscript. The authors declare no other personal or financial relationships that could have influenced this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study used only synthetic records and did not involve human participants or real employee or customer data.

detail.abstract: Across three independent root sets, no handoff-interface effect in parallel multi-agent LLM workflows replicated, and a single-context agent was never dominated on quality and cost. When an orchestrator splits a request across subagents and merges their results, conditional requirements, whose trigger, scope or exception depends on another branch, can be lost at the handoff. In a five-layer preregistered study of more than 4,000 workflows (Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a GPT-5.6-luna subset and a track adapted from TravelPlanner), scored exactly against a finite specification with no LLM judge, we vary whether subagents see the full request or an orchestrator brief, whether handoffs are summaries or structured records, and whether the merger rereads the request. Two measurement artifacts produced apparent effects: the frontier model's effects came from an orchestrator that answered instead of delegating, and a 17-point structured-over-summary effect was measured while the summaries were empty. The single-context agent was the cheapest arm in every family. Rereading at merge helped Qwen3-8B on the original roots (+5.6 points, Holm p = 0.028) but not on fresh roots (+2.4, p = 0.44), where visibility and handoff form reversed direction. A preregistered random-effects meta-analysis found no significant pooled interface effect; visibility and handoff form were heterogeneous (I² = 86% and 87%), and rereading was the only consistent effect (+3.9 points, I² = 0%), with an interval that included zero. Which handoff interface looks better depends more on the task distribution than on the interface. All materials are available from the authors on request.

detail.abstract: The 3-year Integrated National Swine Production Initiatives for Recovery and Expansion (INSPIRE) program is the national repopulation and recovery program of the Philippine Department of Agriculture-National Livestock Program, offering a mix of interventions aimed at reviving the swine industry, which was significantly impacted by African Swine Fever (ASF). The study focused on the interventions provided to the three regions with the highest allocation from fiscal years (FYs) 2022 and 2023: Central Luzon, CALABARZON, and the Davao region. A combination of SARIMA modeling and financial analyses was employed to measure the impacts of the repopulation program. Two forecasts were created: one assumes a situation without African swine fever outbreaks, using datasets from 2000Q1 to 2019Q2, whereas the other reflects the situation prior to the implementation of the INSPIRE program, which utilizes datasets from 2000Q1 to 2021Q4. The study estimated the impact of the INSPIRE program in these three regions, revealing that Central Luzon and CALABARZON significantly benefited from the program. Without the INSPIRE program, pig production in Central Luzon could have been wiped out by the second quarter of 2022 (2022Q2), whereas CALABARZON would have faced a similar scenario by the first quarter of 2023 (2023Q1). In contrast, the INSPIRE program had a lesser impact in the Davao Region, as it was affected by ASF later. The cost benefit analysis and net present value of the program investments yielded favorable ratios that indicate their financial viability and success. Based on the impact analysis, it is recommended that the swine repopulation program be continued beyond 2025 with increased funding. This is the first study in the Philippines which utilizes time series SARIMA forecasting to evaluate the impact of a pig repopulation program.

detail.abstract: When a fund pays departing investors out of the money brought in by arriving ones, the eventual loss is fixed by an accounting identity: whatever the early leavers take out, the late stayers lose. This paper asks who ends up in each group, and answers it with a deliberately small behavioural model. Investors read authorisation as delegated scrutiny, so the probability they attach to undetected misconduct falls with their trust in the supervisor, and exposure is therefore increasing in trust. Verification is costly and is undertaken only when it is rewarded, which makes the set of investors who check an interior region of the trust distribution: those who trust most do not check because they have delegated the screening, and those who trust least may also not check because their positions are too small for verification to pay. Losses fall on the complement of that region and, being proportional to exposure, are borne disproportionately by the most trusting. The distribution of losses is thus an equilibrium object, determined by the same parameter that determined entry. We then add an enforcement stage. Recovering withdrawals acts directly on the promoter's payoff, because that payoff consists entirely of money withdrawn before collapse, and so lowers the penalty needed for deterrence; but applied to ordinary early leavers it also lowers the private return to verification, which is how such schemes are exposed early. Because the recovery share and the probability of recovery enter the deterrence condition multiplicatively, a recovery regime that is unlikely to be applied contributes little deterrence whatever its nominal rate. A final result is uncomfortable for reform design: a new rule raises perceived supervisory effectiveness immediately and actual effectiveness only with a lag, so tightening can widen the trust gap and raise expected losses in the short run.

detail.abstract: Banks' holdings of municipal bonds can induce regulatory forbearance. We establish this fact using U.S. bank balance sheets and enforcement actions over 2002-2019. Our identification strategy instruments banks' holdings with the tax advantages that states offer for investing in municipal bonds. Consistent with public authorities' interest in protecting local government financing, forbearance is stronger among low-capital banks and where weak competitors, illiquid municipal bonds, or greater local government financing needs make bank support more valuable. This effect is stronger among politically connected banks, suggesting that political access helps translate these financing concerns into regulatory accommodation.

detail.abstract: This paper develops an integrated early warning system (EWS) for systemic banking crises that reconciles two paradigms usually treated as rivals: the signal-extraction approach and multivariate probabilistic modelling. In a first stage, the Youden Index selects statistically optimal thresholds that convert continuous macro-financial indicators into binary risk signals. In a second stage, these signals enter a multivariate probit model that aggregates them into a single conditional crisis probability while controlling the macroeconomic environment. Estimated separately for advanced and emerging economies over 1990-2017, the framework uncovers a sharp heterogeneity in the anatomy of systemic risk. In advanced economies, crisis risk is anchored in the credit cycle, where the credit-to-GDP gap and domestic credit dominate. In emerging economies, monetary and liquidity conditions carry the strongest signal, with broad money growth playing the central role. These patterns persist when the Global Financial Crisis window is excluded, which indicates structural regularities rather than an artefact of 2008. The results support an EWS architecture that is interpretable at the indicator level, rigorous at the system level, and explicitly conditioned on country type. The framework is then applied to Morocco. Feeding Moroccan data through the emerging-market model places the country's estimated systemic-crisis probability well below the warning threshold for 2026, with broad money growth some seven percentage points beneath its signalling level, while the same model reflects the elevated monetary pressure that preceded Morocco's 1983 debt crisis.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines selected labour-market trends in India using published Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) estimates, with particular attention to the distinction between overall unemployment and unemployment among educated youth. The analysis uses the usual-status (principal status plus subsidiary status) series for persons aged 15 years and above from 2017–18 to 2023–24, and cross-sectional indicators for 2023–24.

The published unemployment rate for persons aged 15 years and above declined from 6.0 per cent in 2017–18 to 3.2 per cent in 2023–24, while the labour force participation rate rose from 49.8 to 60.1 per cent and the worker population ratio rose from 46.8 to 58.2 per cent. However, the unemployment rate for educated persons (secondary education and above) aged 15 years and above was 7.1 per cent in 2023–24. Among youth aged 15–29, the unemployment rate was 10.2 per cent overall and 15.4 per cent for those with secondary education and above.

The figures illustrate why a single headline unemployment rate is insufficient to describe labour-market conditions. Gender and rural–urban differences, educational transitions, job quality, informality and the distinction between unemployment and non-participation all matter. The paper is descriptive: it does not identify causal effects or independently estimate relationships from unit-level data. It concludes with policy priorities and a reproducible research agenda using PLFS microdata.

detail.abstract: Singapore has built Southeast Asia's clearest compliance market for international carbon credits, yet eligible nature-based supply has barely formed. Projects cannot be financed until host countries authorise exports, and buyers will not contract until credits are eligible; as of November 2025, no credits had been purchased under Singapore's International Carbon Credits framework. This paper proposes a demand-anchored structure to break that deadlock. A price band anchored to Singapore's carbon tax gives buyers and sellers a public ceiling; a Compliance Step-Up Offtake lets buyers contract now at a voluntary price that steps up when credits become eligible; and a Regenerative Demand Note, backed by multilateral first-loss capital, turns signed demand into upfront restoration finance. Corridor sites, or regenerative nodes, pair mangroves and other nature assets with Singapore's energy, food and water imports, with community trusts as contract parties. Scenario modelling sizes Singapore's compliance-anchored demand at 3.2-3.8 MtCO2e a year to 2030, worth about S$110-170 million a year, and about 37 Mt over 2026-2035 in the base case. A review of precedent market structures finds that none yet combines a compliance price anchor, a route to authorisation, finance before eligibility and communities as contract parties. The paper proposes a council of the parties to steward shared rules, shows how a shared ledger and insurers can extend the market, and sets out twenty-one hypotheses and a research agenda for validation.

detail.abstract: Data centers are among the fastest growing sources of electricity demand, yet their effects on agriculture have rarely been examined. We reviewed 61 studies and developed a screening model linking data center electricity demand to on-site and power plant water consumption in four world regions and seven hotspots. Data center water consumption was about 650 billion liters in 2024 and could reach 1,460 billion liters by 2030, 71% of it at power plants. This was under 1% of agricultural water use in every region, but local exposure was substantial. In Virginia, on-site data center water use equaled 13% of irrigation consumption. Exposure through energy appeared larger. US data center demand growth to 2030 exceeded three times total US agricultural electricity use and could raise irrigation pumping costs by USD 150 million to 730 million per year. Siting, cooling choice, reclaimed water and tariff design can limit this exposure.

detail.abstract: Pairwise comparisons of counts after a generalized linear model are usually judged by their multiplicity correction, yet each comparison also needs a valid test. A simulation study of 720 scenarios crossed fourteen inference methods with seven multiplicity procedures under overdispersion, underdispersion, excess zeros, unequal dispersion and unequal group sizes. The inference method governed error control more than the correction. Poisson tests failed under overdispersion, and shared-dispersion models failed when the smallest groups were most dispersed. A robust sandwich test with Welch-type degrees of freedom and Holm's procedure was the most dependable for testing, and a group-wise bootstrap for simultaneous intervals.

detail.abstract: Romania in 2026 is experiencing a systemic crisis driven by the convergence of democratic, economic, and institutional vulnerabilities accumulated over three and a half decades of incomplete transition. The deterioration of representative mechanisms, the fragmentation of public discourse, and the erosion of trust in institutions have transformed democracy into a largely formal framework with diminished practical effectiveness. Macroeconomic imbalances, including a record budget deficit, rising public debt, persistent inflation, and currency depreciation, underscore the fragility of an economic model heavily reliant on consumption and highly exposed to external shocks. The social dimension of the crisis, reflected in declining purchasing power and widening income polarization, further intensifies structural tensions. This analysis demonstrates that the interdependence of political instability, economic vulnerability, and social fragmentation generates a contagion effect that calls into question the state's capacity for recovery and sustainable stabilization.

detail.abstract: Carbon offset markets are increasingly used to reduce the cost of climate mitigation by allowing emissions to be compensated for through abatement elsewhere. However, their effectiveness depends on whether the credits issued represent genuine emission reductions and whether the projects have real benefits to host communities. This paper examines the economics behind carbon offsets alongside the environmental and distributional concerns that limit their effectiveness. It discusses cost-effectiveness as the principal economic justification for offsets, while examining additionality, leakages, and permanence as essential conditions to ensure environmental integrity. It also considers whether offset projects contribute to local development, and how unclear and unresearched the actual development and local involvement are. Finally, this paper evaluates policy responses, including measures to prevent double counting, credit quality standards, community benefit-sharing requirements, and policy-based crediting. The analysis suggests that carbon offsets can offer economic advantages, but these advantages are conditional and do not guarantee genuine reductions or equitable outcomes. Therefore, carbon offset markets should take into consideration environmental integrity as well as economic efficiency.

detail.abstract: This paper measures, as votes are counted, how much investors expect stock values to depend on which candidate wins. Brazil's 2026 presidential election offers two such nights. The same two candidates met in both rounds, the stock exchanges were closed, and the news moved in opposite directions. Combining betting markets with a 24/7 perpetual future on Brazilian stocks, I find that a win by the incumbent president rather than by the challenger lowered the dollar value of Brazilian stocks by 24-30%, ten times US estimates, with the same conservative estimate in both rounds. Betting markets priced the count first. The perpetual, tied to a lagging and apparently capped reference price, followed within minutes on the night it traded actively and more than an hour later on the night it did not.

detail.abstract:
The Endangered Species Committee has a single purpose: to decide whether the stringent protections afforded to species under the Endangered Species Act ("ESA") should be waived. In other words, the six high-level government employees that make up the permanent member so the Committee have the power to decide whether a species will continue on its path to recovery or be written off as dispensable.  It is unsurprising that the Committee is more commonly known as the “God Squad.”

While the God Squad undoubtedly has immense power, that power is not absolute. In fact, the ESA provides procedural and substantive safeguards for the benefit of species at almost every turn. The one exception is 16 U.S.C. § 1536(j), which allows the Secretary of Defense to compel the God Squad to grant an exemption when national security is invoked, regardless of any other provision in the statute.

This provision was used for the first time in March 2026, when the God Squad waived ESA protections for species adversely affected by oil and gas exploration, development, and production activities in the Gulf of Mexico. Lawsuits challenging the God Squad’s decision followed almost immediately (and, in the case of one lawsuit, before the God Squad had even convened). Several of those lawsuits have been dismissed, but some are still pending.

Drawing on the author's experience litigating ESA cases on behalf of the United States, this article offers the first comprehensive examination of the God Squad's national security exemption, its unprecedented use, and the short- and long-term legal and biological implications of the Gulf of Mexico decision.

detail.abstract: Nearly half of U.S. renter households were cost burdened in 2024, and since 2022 one possible contributor has drawn growing legal and political attention: revenue-management software, sold by vendors such as RealPage, that pools non-public lease data from competing landlords and recommends a rent for each unit. Supporters say it helps landlords price accurately; critics say it lets competitors coordinate without communicating, a form of algorithmic collusion that antitrust law, built around agreements, struggles to reach. By October 2026, at least 13 local governments and three states had restricted its use, a fourth state had enacted a ban, and the Department of Justice had proposed a settlement limiting the data that RealPage's leading product may use. This review examines what the software does to rents and what has followed where it has been regulated. The strongest rental study finds that the software makes rents respond faster to demand and estimates a coordination markup of $34 per unit per month, roughly 1.5 to 2 percent of rent. Larger figures exist, but a government estimate of about 4 percent takes its demand elasticities from that same study, and the highest advocacy numbers are allegations from a complaint, not independent analysis. Evidence from other markets, simulations, and laboratory experiments shows that shared algorithms can raise prices but do not always do so. No study located here measures the effect of a local ban, and city rent data could not reveal one, because even a ban that eliminated the markup at every unit could lower average rent by no more than the markup itself. The review therefore proposes a building-level difference-indifferences design that uses the staggered start dates of the laws and can distinguish the efficiency explanation from the coordination one. Shared pricing software probably raises rents modestly; whether bans reduce them will depend on building-level data showing which landlords use it.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how traders respond to algorithmic liquidation in decentralized finance (DeFi), focusing on whether the degree of flexibility embedded in liquidation mechanisms shapes subsequent platform engagement and risk-taking. Using Ethereum event logs from Aave, MakerDAO, and Euler during the Terra/Luna-Celsius and FTX crises of 2022, we compare wallet behavior following fixed-spread and auction-based liquidations. Sixty-day platform abandonment was higher under fixed-spread liquidation in both crises (85.4% vs. 47.2%; 76.3% vs. 52.4%), with the gap persisting after controlling for liquidation size. However, comparisons with non-liquidated peers found no significant liquidation-associated disengagement on Aave but a significant association on MakerDAO. Divergent outcomes between MakerDAO and Euler further suggest that protocol trust may confound mechanism effects. Liquidated wallets resumed borrowing at approximately one-fifth the rate of voluntarily deleveraged peers, contrary to predictions of aggressive re-leveraging. Wallets taking defensive action during peak volatility experienced higher subsequent liquidation rates, potentially reflecting selection bias among already-at-risk positions rather than ineffective risk management. Together, these findings suggest that differences in the flexibility of algorithmic liquidation are associated with subsequent trader behavior, although the independent role of mechanism design remains difficult to isolate from protocol-specific characteristics.

detail.abstract: In February 2026 a war in the Middle East hit the euro area with its second war-driven energy shock in four years. Using the microdata of the ECB Consumer Expectations Survey, we follow the same households before and after the 2022 invasion of Ukraine and the 2026 war. Households raised their one-year-ahead inflation expectations by 2.3 percentage points in both episodes, and at least as much as in 2022 once the change in the inflation they perceived is netted out. Their stated probability that the ECB will maintain price stability fell by a similar amount in both episodes. By July 2026, a month in which oil prices had fallen back before rising again, households had recovered between a third and two thirds of the loss against the same months of 2024, a year without a war, a rebound as large as the one that followed the US tariff announcements of April 2025. By July 2022, with oil prices and inflation still high, they had recovered none of it. Monetary policy is common to the euro area while inflation and fuel prices differ by country, which lets us ask whether households judge the ECB by the inflation they face at home. National inflation has no detectable effect on their stated probability, a bound that rules out large effects though not small ones, and the different paths of the two episodes remain once it is controlled for. Net of years without a war, each point of trust in the ECB lowers the revision of short-term expectations by about 0.1 percentage points. Inflation swaps show the same contrast: the one-year euro area rate gave back two thirds of its rise by July 2026 and none of it by July 2022, while in the United States it fell back in both years. Professional forecasters' longer-term expectations did not move on impact in either episode.

detail.abstract: I assess the Bitcoin price power law as a forecast and as the product of adoption and valuation exponents. On eleven annual origins (2014 to 2024), an expanding power law has log10 root mean squared error (RMSE) of 0.376 and 0.356 at 12 and 24 months, against 0.515 and 0.687 for the last price. Significance depends on the test. The Frisch–Waugh–Lovell theorem gives an exact least-squares identity for the exponent product. On 182 month-ends, the primary product (5.42) is within 1.8% of the time slope (5.52). Across the original four balance-bin proxies and three price series, the shared-trend term equals 99.3 to 99.8% of the product, a signed ratio of fitted coefficients. It has no variance-share interpretation. On the same dates, an added Coin Metrics nonzero-balance stock has a composition gap of 2.1%, versus 13.7% for daily address activity; their signed ratios are 99.48% and 98.58%. The primary partial address coefficient is imprecise. The expanding exponent stays between 5.5 and 6 since 2018. In a post hoc six-proxy, four-penalty grid, all 24 address corrections per price source raise 12-month error and eight lower 24-month error relative to the expanding power law. All evidence is retrospective and leaves the mechanism unidentified.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Arbitral Decision-making: When can an Award be Challenged because AI Materially Influenced the Tribunal's Reasoning? -Chinonso Ekuma

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence in Arbitral Decision-making: When can an Award be Challenged because AI Materially Influenced the Tribunal's Reasoning? -Chinonso Ekuma

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known personal, financial or professional relationships or competing interests that could have influenced, or be perceived to have influenced, the conduct of this research.

detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being deployed by arbitrators in legal research, analytical processes, and in drafting arbitral awards. The use of generative AI, however, raises a question that, although increasingly addressed by soft-law instruments, remains judicially unresolved, essentially whether an arbitral award may be set aside, or its recognition and enforcement refused, where AI has materially influenced the tribunal’s reasoning. The first judicial test of this issue, LaPaglia v Valve Corp, was dismissed in December 2025 on jurisdictional grounds, without determination of the substantive questions raised. This article argues that there is no need to establish a separate ground for challenging AI-assisted arbitral awards, as existing legal frameworks are capable of addressing defects arising from the use of AI in arbitral proceedings. Existing legal frameworks, such as the UNCITRAL Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration, the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (New York Convention), and the Arbitration Act 1996 (England and Wales), provide a sufficient basis for addressing AI-related procedural and substantive irregularities. The central challenge is to articulate the relevance of AI’s influence through established legal concepts, particularly the abdication of the arbitrator’s independent decision-making function, reliance on material outside the evidential record without affording the parties an opportunity to respond, and reasoning that discloses a failure to engage independently with the parties’ submissions and evidence. Drawing on P v Q, the Yukos set-aside proceedings, Soh Beng Tee & Co Pte Ltd v Fairmount Development Pte Ltd, and DJP v DJO, the article contends that breaches of the right to be heard provide the most viable basis for challenging AI-assisted awards. By contrast, challenges founded on improper delegation of the adjudicative function are likely to encounter significant evidential and doctrinal obstacles, particularly where the arbitrator has formally adopted and signed the award, thereby assuming responsibility for its contents. The article concludes that the most effective response lies not in creating a novel ground of challenge, but in strengthening procedural safeguards governing the use of AI in arbitral proceedings. These should include agreed protocols regulating the use of AI, appropriate disclosure where AI-generated material introduces information beyond the evidential record, independent verification of AI-generated outputs, and adequate record-keeping to preserve accountability and facilitate subsequent judicial scrutiny.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the long-term impacts of large-scale manufacturing transfer on human capital, leveraging the quasi-random placement of the Soviet-aided 156 Projects in China. Using staggered DID and instrumental variable strategies with manually collected data, I find that the projects increased educational attainment and reduced intergenerational educational persistence, but lowered returns to schooling. A general equilibrium model of the dual economy, supported by structural estimation, identifies wage incentives and labor reallocation as key mechanisms. Counterfactual analysis shows that the actual allocation reduced regional inequality at the cost of aggregate efficiency. The results reveal the dual legacy of heavy-industry-oriented development.

title: Beyond the Digital Development/Colonialism Binary: The Structural and Institutional Ordering of Technological Power, Dependence, and Inequality

detail.title: Beyond the Digital Development/Colonialism Binary: The Structural and Institutional Ordering of Technological Power, Dependence, and Inequality

declarations.declarationOfInterest: n/a

detail.abstract: The global expansion of the digital economy is marked by deep tensions. On one hand, internet connectivity and infrastructure are dominated by multinational tech corporations, reinforcing dependence and exploitation in the Global South. On the other, closing the digital divide remains a global imperative. This raises a critical question: are connectivity, domination, and dependence inevitable, or can there be a path toward non-exploitative inclusion? While existing scholarship on the constitution of global inequality has examined the role of colonial legacies, neoliberalism, international law, and transnational corporate governance, it has largely overlooked the structural role of technology, an issue of increased relevance today. Emerging discourses — “digital development” and “digital colonialism”— acknowledge technology’s impact but are presently disconnected, leading to questions of connectivity and inclusion being treated separately from questions of multinational power and exploitation, which ought to be considered together. These discourses also remain limited in other ways: “digital development” depoliticizes digitalization, while “digital colonialism” treats tech-driven domination as novel. This article engages both frameworks, and critiques them for their ahistoricism: the dynamics surrounding technology dependence in development struggles accompanied by multinational power and exploitation are not new issues that we are tackling for the first time in the digital era. These issues have a history, and they are institutionally and structurally encoded into the global order. This article argues that envisioning justice in the digital economy requires grounding technological power within long-standing legal and economic structures. By tracing the historical co-production of global inequality through technology and legal institutions, this article offers a framework for understanding contemporary dynamics and identifying pathways toward global justice.

detail.abstract: This paper examines historical reports concerning the administration of Sawad in early Islamic Iraq, focusing on the decision attributed to Umar ibn al-Khattab not to distribute its agricultural lands among the conquering troops, the reported land-tax assessments, and transmitted revenue figures. Using al-Baladhuri in Philip K. Hitti's English translation alongside modern scholarship, the study distinguishes historical testimony from interpretations of policy rationale and from claims about economic outcomes. The source reports a survey of 36 million jaribs, assessments combining money and in-kind payments, and several large kharaj totals. However, these reports do not establish a uniform tariff across all land, a verified series of comparable annual collections, or the settlement's precise effects on agricultural production, cultivator welfare, net revenue, or long-term fiscal sustainability. The paper argues that the evidence supports analysis of the reported landholding and taxation arrangement, but not a conclusive verdict on its economic performance. It identifies the further source comparison and contextual evidence needed to test stronger claims.

detail.abstract:
«Fundamentals of Healthcare Marketing» sets out to describe the first organic academic systematisation of healthcare marketing in Italy, a discipline which, despite being central to the communication, management and positioning processes of healthcare organisations, has never received a unified and scientifically grounded treatment in the national literature. 

The work integrates economic, legal, communicative and digital perspectives, offering a complete theoretical-methodological framework that fills a significant disciplinary gap.

The volume reconstructs the regulatory evolution of healthcare communication from Law No. 175/1992 to Law No. 248/2006, up to the most recent regulatory provisions, analysing the relationship between liberalisation, patient protection and professional liability. 

This dimension is complemented by an extensive treatment of the economic and market fundamentals of the healthcare sector, with particular attention to quasi-market models, patient decision-making processes and the specific nature of health as the supreme good.

The work also introduces an original contribution in the field of regulated communication, integrating semiotics, anthropology, digital advertising and YMYL/E‑E‑A‑T principles, and proposing an interpretive model that connects healthcare communication to the contemporary paradigms of digital reputation, informational transparency and reputational risk management. 

The framework is completed by an advanced analysis of digital platforms, bidding systems and healthcare media mixes, together with a reflection on physician-patient communication, reference markets and the management of communication crises in clinical settings.

The text is intended as a reference for university education in healthcare management, scientific communication, health economics and digital health, offering a solid, up-to-date and interdisciplinary theoretical framework suited to master's degree courses, second-level master's programmes and advanced training pathways for professionals and executives in the sector.

detail.abstract: Observers frequently interpret the divergence of short-term sovereign bond yields from official targets ahead of scheduled central bank announcements as a symptom of impaired liquidity management that can have significant implications for monetary policy transmission. The present study evaluates this assumption within the context of Pakistan, exploring the alternative hypothesis that such deviations instead reflect the market expectations of the future path of policy rate based on macroeconomic news and central bank communication. The analysis uses on daily Pakistan Revaluation (PKRV) Treasury bill yields across multiple tenors from May 2015 through October 2026, evaluated within a 15-trading-day window around scheduled policy announcements. To ground the empirical observations, the paper introduces a discrete-time term-structure model accounting for Interest Rate Corridor liquidity frictions, heterogeneous private expectations, and Bayesian signal extraction. The methodological framework addresses common emerging-market constraints by shifting from thinly traded 1-month tenors to the more liquid 3-month benchmark, employing bootstrapped local projections and penalized regression techniques to accommodate small sample sizes. Textual analysis of monetary policy statements separates forecast-based information proxies from commitment-based forward guidance. Estimates suggest that while pre-meeting yield spreads generally widen in anticipation of rate adjustments, they tend to narrow rapidly within five trading days after a decision takes effect. Explicit Odyssean commitment language is associated with lower pre-announcement dispersion and faster post-decision anchoring. Ultimately, the findings indicate that secondary market yield movements ahead of policy meetings likely reflect rational price discovery rather than a fundamental breakdown in monetary transmission.

detail.abstract: This chapter examines bureaucratic inertia (懒政怠政 lanzheng daizheng) in the People's Republic of China and its consequences for administrative justice, focusing on the campaign against 'lying flat style officials' (躺平 式干部 tangping shi ganbu) that came into public view in 2023. The Party diagnoses inertia chiefly as individual failing: wrong consciousness, weak commitment and lapses in discipline. The chapter argues that the principal causes are instead institutional and structural. Excessive and meaningless work at the local level, performance and veto targets, the costs and risks of campaigns, fragmented jurisdiction and powers, liability and lifetime accountability regimes, and citizen-generated supervision together raise the costs and risks of exercising administrative power. Official responses combine ideological education with burden reduction, expanded and increasingly interchangeable Party and state sanctions, and a limited extension of administrative litigation and review to omissions. The case illustrates two features of contemporary Chinese governance: the merging of governance by law, governance by virtue and personalised rule; and the interdependence of, and tension between, bureaucratic and mobilisational modes of administration. A campaign against inertia caused in part by meetings, reports and inspections is itself implemented through meetings, reports and inspections. Citizens bear the cost, in diminished services and limited redress.

detail.abstract: Buy now, pay later (BNPL) is increasingly popular among U.S. consumers, but the share of users who made late BNPL payments-a sign of overextension-has also increased more recently. A few states have begun regulating BNPL lenders and imposing a requirement to perform stricter assessments of consumers' repayment abilities. Such a requirement may affect consumers with elevated financial vulnerability because they may be at greater risks of overextension as well as receiving meaningful benefits from using BNPL. In this paper, we use data from the 2025 Survey of Household Economics and Decisionmaking to analyze how consumers' financial vulnerability is associated with BNPL use and late payments. Additionally, we conduct counterfactual policy experiments to examine how the requirement of stricter assessments may affect BNPL use by current users with and without late payments. We find that highly and moderately financially vulnerable consumers are significantly more likely to use BNPL compared with financially healthy consumers even after controlling for all other variables, but conditional on BNPL use, only highly financially vulnerable consumers are significantly more likely to make late BNPL payments. Our counterfactual experiments show that BNPL lenders' stricter assessments may help reduce overextension risks by restricting BNPL access for those who would make late payments; however, such assessments may also have a nontrivial unintended consequence of restricting BNPL access for those who would repay the loan on time. Both intended and unintended consequences may fall mostly on highly financially vulnerable consumers.

detail.abstract: This special issue centers on the economic implications of two powerful demographic trends: falling birth rates and longer life spans. While many advanced economies face these shifts, South Korea’s experience is unique in its speed and intensity. It serves as an urgent case study for the rest of the world. In just a few decades, Korea transformed from a young society with high fertility into one with the lowest birth rates globally and a rapidly aging population. Korea’s total fertility rate dropped to a record low of 0.72 in 2023. At the same time, life expectancy has risen so fast that Korea’s old-age dependency ratio is expected to pass Japan’s by 2050. These changes create massive challenges for government budgets, labor markets, and family structures. Economists have long tried to explain why fertility falls as countries get richer. Early theories, like the “quantity-quality” trade-off, argued that as income rises, parents choose to have fewer children but invest more in each one.

detail.abstract: This paper explores the relationship between socioeconomic status (SES) and the recent rapid decline in marriage rates in China and South Korea, using nationally representative longitudinal data. The analysis shows that recently rising never-married rates (NVMR) are increasingly concentrated among lower-SES individuals, especially in highly urbanised areas in both countries, highlighting the growing significance of financial barriers to family formation in recent years. Furthermore, income has become a stronger predictor of marriage entry by men in both nations. The overall rise in the NVMR reflects delayed marriage among the Chinese population and Korean women, but more persistent singlehood among lower-SES Korean men aged over 35. Notably, the faster growth of the NVMR among lower-SES groups has narrowed overall SES differences in marriage rates, eroding the historical pattern in which lower-SES individuals married earlier and more universally. In other words, marriage differentials based on SES are disappearing on absolute levels. This suggests that while financial constraints remain a key influence, broader structural and cultural shifts — such as evolving gender norms and rising opportunity costs — are also critical for understanding recent marriage declines in East Asia.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the role of ‘healthy aging’ in boosting labor supply in Korea. First, we use microdata from surveys to assess whether there is evidence that the physical abilities of individuals aged 50 years and above have been improving over successive cohorts. Second, we investigate whether health improvements among older workers influence their labor market outcomes, such as the decision to supply labor or to retire. We use an instrumental variable approach to enable causal inference, proxying exogenous variations in health with the incidence of certain chronic diseases. Our findings reveal that (i) physical health indicators have improved on average across birth cohorts, providing evidence in favor of ‘healthy aging’ in Korea, and (ii) better health increases the probability of participating in the labor force and postponing retirement. Overall, our results suggest that healthy aging increased the labor supply of older individuals in Korea by around 1.9 percentage points per year during the period 2006-20. The results for Korea are qualitatively comparable but quantitatively somewhat stronger than those for comparator Asian countries.

detail.abstract:
Key findings:
– The twin ecological and digital transitions are giving rise to widespread anxiety, particularly concerning job and economic security. Concerns about the effects of climate policies and digitalisation are distinct but closely connected. Indeed, while climate measures are often perceived as threatening livelihoods and established ways of life, digital transformation fosters fears of automation, job displacement and economic insecurity.
– Populist actors are aggressively exploiting these anxieties for electoral gain. They portray climate policies as elite-driven projects that impose unfair costs on ordinary people, while also amplifying fears about job losses and declining security linked to digital transformation. In this way they turn real transition-related concerns into political resentment.
– Anxiety about the twin transitions is associated with a lowering of the perceived importance of democracy and more virulent populist positions. People who are concerned about these transformations tend to attach less importance to democracy and also espouse more radical populist views. In several European countries, they are even significantly more likely to consider supporting far-right political parties. Such concerns are particularly prevalent among low-income groups, but also, interestingly, union members.
– Workplaces are an important arena for reducing transition-related insecurity and strengthening democratic resilience. Stronger economic citizenship rights, better working conditions and institutionalised opportunities for workers to exercise voice can help to mitigate anxieties linked to these twin transitions. By addressing insecurity at work, such measures can also reduce susceptibility to far-right populist appeals.

detail.abstract: Despite the European Union's ambitious plans to secure critical raw materials and defense spending of approximately €900 billion by 2030, Europe remains heavily dependent on China for rare earth processing. This dependency particularly affects high-performance permanent magnets, which are indispensable for modern weapon systems, AI infrastructure, and space technology. The dependency does not stem from a lack of raw material deposits, but from a self-imposed regulatory dilemma. Strict European environmental, due diligence, and supply chain regulations prevent the establishment of large-scale domestic processing capacities and shift the most environmentally intensive process steps to China. The article develops a theoretical framework combining extended dependency theory and securitization theory to distinguish performative from effective resource security. A global comparison of strategies pursued by the EU, USA and China shows that only the USA has significantly improved its supply security through direct state investments, regulatory exemptions, and projects such as Golden Dome, yet without initially achieving complete independence. Without targeted deregulation for strategically important projects, investments in large-scale refining and infrastructure, and pragmatic partnerships, the aspired strategic autonomy remains largely symbolic worldwide, except in China. In particular, Europe faces considerable security risks to its defense capabilities, artificial intelligence development, and space technologies.

detail.abstract: Population aging reduces the supply of potential entrepreneurs, contributing to the secular decline in business dynamism. At the same time, aging reshapes bank funding: older households save disproportionately in deposits, easing local credit conditions. We study how these countervailing forces shape the entry and quality of new firms. Using data on U.S. cities from 1978-2021 and an instrumental variable based on historical age structure, we confirm that aging depresses local firm entry. Yet this decline is about one-third weaker in bank-dependent sectors, consistent with aging-induced deposit inflows relaxing local borrowing constraints. The additional entrants in these sectors are smaller, less likely to survive, and pay lower relative wages, suggesting that this credit-sustained entry comes at the cost of entrepreneurial quality.

detail.abstract: This paper challenges the widespread view that existing WTO rules are insufficient for dealing with state capitalism in China, which has been further emboldened by the latest rounds of state-owned enterprise (“SOE”) reforms. Through a careful review of WTO agreements and jurisprudence, it is argued that new rules are not necessarily needed because the unique challenges created by China’s state capitalism can be appropriately addressed by the WTO’s existing rules on subsidies coupled with the China-specific obligations. A more realistic approach would be to encourage China to undertake market-oriented reforms through WTO litigation based on existing rules rather than trying to negotiate new rules.

detail.abstract: Employing proprietary individual-level financial transactions data from one of the UK's largest commercial banks, we investigate how socioeconomic factors moderate the evolution of financial vulnerability. Drawing on hundreds of millions of observations capturing the earnings and consumption decisions of 698,688 active accounts between 2019 and 2023 and using Russia's war in Ukraine as an exogenous shock, we identify the causal moderating effect of income level on financial vulnerability. We document economically substantial effects based on changes to metrics-based interactions between income and expenditure. Within-month spending volatility rises by 64.7% for low-income relative to higher-income individuals, underscoring the constraints low-income households face with regard to smoothing consumption. Controlling for additional income sources also widens the expenditure-to-income differential from 2.8% to 5.0%. Individuals reliant on pensions and benefits exhibit vulnerability comparable to low-income groups.

detail.abstract: Green branding has been gathering momentum, permeating different markets and industrial sectors. It also represents a valuable perspective to study the ongoing transformations in trademark law driven by sustainability imperatives and increasing automation. Focusing on the European Union, the chapter explores the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in the governance of green trademarks. In particular, we take a close look at trademark registration, cancellation, and the governance of certification trademarks, as key areas to enhance the EU green trademarks landscape. The analysis unveils a promising role of AI in assisting human legal assessment. The introduction of ad hoc AI systems may help IP offices build meaningful datasets, identify potentially descriptive and deceptive green trademarks applications, monitor the truthfulness of successfully registered ones, and solidly support green certification trademarks as a core mechanism to align EU trademark law with consumer protection and environmental policies.

detail.abstract: What scientists choose not to publish can be as important as what they do publish.We measure missing research results at the hypothesis level and use this approach to study under-reporting in economics. Across 5,057 pre-registered hypotheses from 317 studies registered on the American Economic Association RCT Registry between 2015 and 2017, only 42% have publicly available results eight to nine years after pre-registration. Among the available results, 64% are null, and we find little evidence that null results are disproportionately missing. In an RCT, direct engagement with authors increases the share of hypotheses with available results by 6.2 percentage points, while raising awareness alone has no significant effect and additional research assistance provides no further improvement. Direct engagement also increases explanations for unavailable results, reducing the share of hypotheses that remain unaccounted for by 16.4 percentage points. The findings document extensive under-reporting in economics that does not appear to be driven primarily by the suppression of null results, and suggest that reporting pre-registered results may need to become a standard part of the research process rather than something recovered years later.

detail.title: The conditions of legal protections. A counterfactual analysis of workers' data protection rights under the Digital Omnibus and Digital Omnibus on AI

publicationDetails.detailsText: ETUI Research Paper - Working Paper 2026.05
publicationDetails.journalName: European Trade Union Institute (ETUI) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This working paper examines how the European Union Digital Omnibus proposal and the adopted Digital Omnibus on AI may affect worker data protection and the enforceability of digital rights at work. It focuses on three connected dimensions: workers' ability to obtain information and exercise their rights; the continuing legal effectiveness of the provisions of the General Data Protection Regulation after the Omnibus amendments; and the capacity of data protection authorities to detect, investigate and enforce. The paper applies a counterfactual method to four workplace cases – Amazon France Logistique, H&M, Uber and Ola (as a joint case), and Foodinho/Glovo – holding the original facts and evidence constant. The outcomes in three of these cases remain broadly comparable, but rights are weakened in that of Uber and Ola. The absence of displaced outcomes should not be read as evidence of the omnibuses having limited effect: the counterfactual tests legal protection once the facts and evidence are already available, but captures less well whether similar practices that might be the subject of complaint may afterwards become harder to discover, document and challenge. The study finds that the main risk arises from the combined effects of weaker access to information, changes to the legal basis for challenge and the existing limits on enforcement capacity.

detail.abstract: Accuracy is a performance measure to evaluate the effectiveness of a classification model, it measures the overall correctness of an algorithm's predictions regarding the class labels. This article shows that pattern recognition algorithms are inaccurate, in the sense that they are myopic: they only recognise objects that are close to their training sets. The reason for this is that in order to process large volumes of data, the data must first be compressed. Compression is achieved through feature extraction to obtain a lower dimensional representation of the training data. It is assumed that these features represent the relevant underlying factors that explain the data, and that the other data characteristics can therefore be disregarded. The problem, however, is that what is considered relevant is determined in relation to the original training set. The consequence of this is that the algorithm became blind to new relevant information about the objects.

detail.abstract: I examine a class of continuous-state cheap talk games where the receiver is uncertain about the preferences of the sender. Only one of the two sender types (a "good" type) can meaningfully communicate with the receiver; the other will only induce the highest possible action (a "bad" type). I study the two-period version of this game, where the state changes each period but the sender's type is persistent. I show that high levels of reputation are detrimental to communication, but due to a distinct mechanism: the good sender chooses to send a revealing message in every state, which is not possible due to the bad sender's incentives. This causes collapses in communication to be discontinuous with respect to the value of reputation. At lower levels of reputation, communication improves only if the good sender is misaligned with the receiver; at high reputation levels, no informative communication can occur in the first period. Further, communication may actually be more informative when the good sender and receiver are partially misaligned. I show similar results hold in the finite-horizon case.

detail.abstract: Our Data Descriptor documents the geocoding of raw applicant and inventor address data available in EPO and PCT patent applications in the 2026 REGPAT release to provide a dataset of international patenting activity across 35 countries, harmonised to the European Commission's Global Human Settlement Layer 1 km 2 grids. It covers 3,240,581 patent families from 2000 onwards, increasing the granularity of subnational analysis from 1,971 TL3 regions to 901,054 1 km 2 grid cells. To handle locational uncertainty where full address information is not available, we recover street lengths and postcode boundaries, or where unavailable, reverse geocode postcodes using a flood-fill algorithm, weighting these values by epoch-specific built environment characteristics at 100 m grid detail to interpolate their plausible locations. The resulting data provide a transparent, lightweight and updatable basis for analysing the rapidly evolving fine-scale geography of inventive activity while retaining spatial uncertainty of the underlying address evidence.

detail.abstract: Non-compete covenants are an issue of particular concern in developed economies. While traditionally these covenants were allowed to protect employer investments that were appropriable when the employee left, the growth in the use of these covenants in recent years has given rise to the concern that they increase employer labor market power decreasing labor mobility, wages, and economic efficiency. This Article examines the prevalence of non-compete covenants and their growing significance in the United States and Europe. We review the economic literature on the impact of non-compete covenants on employer investment and labor market power, and the corresponding evidence of their impact on labor mobility, wages, efficiency, and consumer welfare. This Article conducts a novel review of existing empirical research to compare differences in regulatory efforts between common law and civil law jurisdictions. Additionally, this Article explores approaches to non-competes under antitrust law and competitions policy. This discussion includes an examination of the Federal Trade Commission's proposed 2024 ban on most non-compete agreements and its potential to alter labor dynamics. This Article concludes by recommending areas for future research. Forthcoming in the Hofstra Labor and Employment Law Journal.
